audits.published_statement: WEC: T_ab xi^a xi^b >= 0 for every timelike xi (Curiel p.6; MM&V eq 2.5; K&S eq 18). NEC: T_ab k^a k^b >= 0 for every null k (MM&V eq 2.6). SEC: (T_ab - T g_ab/2) xi^a xi^b >= 0 for every timelike xi (4D; K&S eq 20 gives T/(n-2) in n dimensions). DEC: T_ab xi^a xi^b >= 0 AND -T^a_b xi^b causal and future-directed for every timelike xi; equivalently T_ab t^a xi^b >= 0 for co-oriented timelike t, xi. Implications: 'Clearly, the SDEC implies the DEC, which implies the WEC' (Curiel p.8); 'if the WEC is not satisfied, then the DEC has to be violated. However, the WEC and the SEC are, in principle, completely independent' (MM&V p.3); 'the DEC is just the combination of the WEC and the FEC' (MM&V p.13); 'even though the name suggests it, the SEC does not imply the WEC' (K&S p.9). Type-I effective forms: NEC rho+p_i>=0; WEC adds rho>=0; SEC adds rho+Sum p_i>=0; DEC |p_i|<=rho, rho>=0 (MM&V p.6).
published_hypotheses: These are definitions, not theorems. They quantify over ALL timelike (resp. null) vectors at a point: 'holds' needs every observer, 'fails' needs only one.
4-dimensional Lorentzian (M,g) with signature (-,+,+,+). The SEC's 1/2 is the n=4 value of 1/(n-2).
The Hawking-Ellis DEC includes the WEC clause. The flux-only condition (FEC, MM&V eq 4.3) is a different condition and does NOT imply the WEC.
The effective (rho, p_i) forms require Hawking-Ellis type I. The covariant forms need no type assumption.
The physical form equals the geometric form only when the Einstein equation holds (Curiel p.5). T_ab = G_ab in certify.py's units is exactly that identification.
hypothesis_drift: WEAKENED NAME, certify.py:353-355. dec_holds(wec_min) = wec_min >= 0 is only the NECESSARY half of the DEC. The published DEC also needs the flux -T^a_b V^b to be causal (z3 counterexample: rho=0, p_i=1/2 satisfies the WEC and fails the DEC). The tree uses it only in the published direction (WEC fails => DEC fails; certify.py:85, :453), and every sampled WEC minimum is negative, so no printed verdict is affected. The DEC column at certify.py:450 would still print 'ok' for a tensor that satisfies the WEC and violates the DEC. This is a discrepancy, not a refutation.

ADDED SAMPLING, certify.py:336-351. The published WEC/SEC quantify over all timelike vectors; the tree samples 200 Fibonacci directions x speeds j/11, j=1..10. The static observer s=0 is not in the sample, and the cap s=10/11 excludes s->1. One negative sample is a valid witness of violation, so 'VIOLATED' stands. The sampled minima are NOT infima: where rho+p<0 the WEC infimum over observers is -infinity (K&S Prop 2.1; Le 2602.18023 sec 2.2). Measured at r=1: gamma^2(rho+s^2 p) = -4.66e-3 at s=10/11, -4.39e-2 at s=0.99, -4.41e2 at s=0.999999. The tree's own hypothesis list already names this.

ADDED, certify.py:321-323. The orthonormal static tetrad e = diag(1/sqrt(-g00), 1/sqrt(gii)) is valid only for a diagonal metric. The conformastatic metric is diagonal and its Einstein tensor is exactly diagonal (type I) in that frame (sympy, this audit), so this drift has no effect here.
SEC at certify.py:336-351 uses w + T/2 with T = eta^mn T_mn. Machine-checked equal to (T_ab - T g_ab/2)V^aV^b for unit timelike V (sympy). Valid only at n=4, which is the tree's dimension. No drift.

overturn.py:207-213. 'rho < 0 ... means the POINTWISE weak energy condition fails' holds by definition when rho is the energy density T_ab u^a u^b measured by some timelike u. The file's density is a functional, not a solution of the field equations (stated at overturn.py:209-211), so the implicit hypothesis is 'rho is an observer-measured T_ab u^a u^b'. Under that reading there is no drift, and 'flat-space kinematics' is not needed for the implication.

later_literature.what: Table 1 / Fig. 2: DEC => WEC => NEC, SEC => NEC, and the SEC does not imply the WEC. Prop 2.1: a scale-invariant EC bounded below has infimum 0, so a WEC violation makes the sampled minimum unbounded below. All pointwise ECs are violated by QFT and by nonminimal classical scalars. That is a statement about the ECs as physical laws, not about the definitions the tree uses.
DEC = WEC + FEC. The FEC alone is independent of the sign of rho. Gives type I-IV tables and calls the ECs 'provisional' as fundamental physics.
Gives the definitions in geometric, physical and effective forms: 'SDEC implies the DEC, which implies the WEC'. The DEC and SDEC effective forms coincide only for type I.

later_literature.ref: Le, 'Observer-robust energy condition verification for warp drive spacetimes', arXiv:2602.18023 (2026)
later_literature.what: An S-lemma LMI decides NEC/WEC/SEC/DEC exactly (Thm 1: DEC = WEC for T and for -T^2). 'A negative value witnesses WEC violation; a nonnegative capped value does not prove WEC.' Finite Fibonacci sampling detected only 93.4% of DEC violations at 10^3 directions (Rodal). This narrows sampled SATISFACTION claims, not sampled VIOLATION claims, and certify.py makes only the latter.

audits.lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested. These are DEFINITIONS plus one logical implication. They contain no measured input, so no datum that became available later can move them. Evidence: the same definitions and the same DEC=>WEC implication are restated unchanged in 2014, 2017, 2020 and 2026 (sources above), and DEC=>WEC is re-derived here by z3 (type I) and by a covariant sampled check (no type assumption). What later work did add concerns two other things. First, the ECs' status as physical constraints: violation by quantum fields (K&S sec 2.3, 'all pointwise energy conditions are necessarily violated by essentially any QFT') and the abandonment of the trace EC after Zel'dovich (MM&V p.3-5). Second, how to test the ECs numerically (Le 2026). Neither bears on the tree's use: certify.py and overturn.py use the ECs as diagnostics of a given T_ab and certify only violations, which need one witness. Evidence the other way: none found. No later paper revises the definitions or the implication.

They also match the direction of 'the DEC requires the WEC' that the tree actually uses: WEC fails => DEC fails, z3-valid, with 0 exceptions among 234 DEC-satisfying tensors in the covariant check. The violation claims at certify.py:84-85 are reproduced from an independent exact sympy Einstein tensor at all six radii, and the closed form extends them to every 0<r<R_s. Three discrepancies are recorded; none is a refutation and none moves the conclusion. (1) dec_holds() is named as the DEC but is only its necessary WEC half (certify.py:353-355). (2) Sampled minima are not infima; the tree names this itself. (3) certify.py:96-97 quotes the coordinate T_00 (-4.8455e-4, ratio 1.21) where the orthonormal value is -4.6564e-4 (ratio 1.1655), and the selftest at :456 cannot catch it because near() uses an absolute tolerance when |want| < 1 (:411). verifiers.reason:
I could not refute the grade in either direction. One small inaccuracy in the audit's own discrepancy note is recorded below. It does not move the grade.

SOURCES, READ VIA alphaXiv
- Curiel 1405.0403, p.6 table and p.8. The table matches the audit's definitions in geometric, physical and effective forms. The DEC physical form includes the WEC clause. The text says "The SEC does not imply the WEC" and "Clearly, the SDEC implies the DEC, which implies the WEC."
- Martin-Moruno & Visser 1702.05915. Eqs 2.3-2.6 and "if the WEC is not satisfied, then the DEC has to be violated. However, the WEC and the SEC are, in principle, completely independent" are on PDF p.4 (printed p.3). The type-I table is on p.6. "by its very definition the DEC is just the combination of the WEC and the FEC" is on printed p.13. All match.
- Kontou & Sanders 2003.01815. Eq 18 (WEC) and eq 20 (SEC with T/(n-2)) match. So do "even though the name suggests it, the SEC does not imply the WEC" (p.9), Table 1, and Props 2.1-2.2 (p.11).
- Le 2602.18023 v6. Eqs 2-5 match, and so does Thm 1(4): the DEC holds iff the WEC holds for T and for -(T^2). The p.9 quote "A negative value witnesses WEC violation; a nonnegative capped value does not prove WEC" is verbatim. The 93.4% figure: p.19 says "at 10^3 directions", and the Fig. 4 caption counts it as 10^4 observer samples (10 rapidities each). The two are consistent.
- Hawking-Ellis 1973 was not read by me either. NAMED-NOT-READ is the correct status, and three independent restatements agree.

INDEPENDENT MACHINE CHECK
I wrote a separate sympy script (verify/refute/ec-defs-indep.py). It builds the Einstein tensor of g = diag(-e^{2Phi}, e^{-2Phi} delta) from Christoffels in Cartesian coordinates, at r=1 on the x-axis, with m=a=0.02 and Phi shifted by -m/R_s. It does not reuse the auditor's code. Results:
- In the static tetrad the tensor is exactly diagonal (type I). All off-diagonal entries are 0.
- rho = -4.656372516e-4, p_r = -4.157386e-4, p_t = +4.157386e-4.
- rho+p_r = -8.814e-4, rho+p_t = -4.990e-5, rho+Sum p = -4.990e-5, all negative.
- The coordinate component is T_00 = -4.845395e-4.
These confirm the audit's closed forms. rho+p_t equals 2e^{2Phi} lap Phi, with lap Phi = -3ma^2/(r^2+a^2)^{5/2} < 0. So the NEC, WEC and SEC fail, and with them the DEC. (Remark: the same Laplacian also holds for r > R_s, since -m/r is harmonic. The audit's restriction to 0<r<R_s is conservative, not wrong.)

TREE CHECKS
- The auditor's rederive script exits 0 with ALL CHECKS PASS.
- certify.py --selftest prints 'T_00 at r = 1  -0.000465643  -0.00048455  ok'. That confirms the vacuous near() tolerance the audit describes at certify.py:409-411 and :456.
- dec_holds and energy_conditions are used only inside certify.py (:450, :453). No other board file calls certify.dec_holds or certify.energy_conditions; the importers use only phi, contracts, theorem_holds, THEOREM_SCOPE, orthonormal, stress_energy and similar. So the WEC-only DEC proxy is never used as a certificate that the DEC holds. That is the audit's stated NARROWED trigger, and it is not met.
- The SEC formula w + T/2 is correct at n=4.
- The NEC vector k=(1,u) is null in the orthonormal frame.

REFUTE-TOWARD-NARROWED
This fails. Every use is in the valid direction (WEC fails => DEC fails). Every claim is a violation claim resting on a negative witness, and the exact closed form strengthens it.

REFUTE-TOWARD-WRONG/OPEN
This fails. The definitions carry no datum, so there is nothing a later measurement could move. Every restatement I read (2014, 2017, 2020, 2026) agrees.

ONE INACCURACY IN THE AUDIT (a discrepancy, not a refutation)
The audit corrects certify.py:97's 'ratio of 1.21' to 'the orthonormal ratio is 1.1655'. But 1.1655 is itself frame-mixed: it divides the orthonormal rho by the flat-coordinate Phi'^2 = 3.9952e-4. The tree's 1.21 is also mixed: coordinate T_00 over flat Phi'^2.
- A frame-consistent ratio is rho_hat / (e^{2Phi} Phi'^2) = 1 + 2|lap Phi|/Phi'^2 = 1.1200. Here e^{2Phi} Phi'^2 = g^{rr} Phi'^2 is the orthonormal gradient squared, which equals |p_r|.
- So the tree's figure needs a frame label, not a replacement by 1.1655.
- The dominance claim ('a SQUARE carrying a minus sign') holds under every reading, since the square makes up about 89% of rho.
- Suggested rewording of discrepancy (3): the -4.8455e-4 value is coordinate, not orthonormal, so the selftest compares unlike quantities. 1.21 and 1.1655 are both frame-mixed ratios, and the frame-consistent ratio is 1.1200.
The remaining audit claims check out against source and computation: the coordinate-vs-orthonormal T_00 discrepancy, the vacuous selftest tolerance, sampled minima not being infima, the WEC-only dec_holds name, and SEAT_LEAD_SPLIT_SURVIVES resting only on exact signs.

The other dec_holds functions (stability.py, membrane.py) are separate functions, as the audit says.

ENCODING CHECK:
- (A) The z3 type-I forms match MM&V's table. The DEC is rho >= |p_i|. The FEC is rho^2 >= p_i^2, which is correct for type I: the flux F = gamma(rho, s p n) is causal for every s < 1 iff p^2 <= rho^2.
- DEC=>WEC is definitional in Hawking-Ellis, and the audit says so. Since that implication is not empirical, a z3 proof of it is appropriate.
- (B) checks the SEC contraction only for V in the xy-plane. The identity (T_ab - T g_ab/2)V^aV^b = w + T/2 holds for any unit timelike V, so this is a narrower proof than possible, not a wrong one.
- (C) is an independent exact Einstein tensor of exactly certify.py's conformastatic metric. Phi = m/sqrt(r^2+a^2) - m/max(r,R_s), as at certify.py:200-201. It agrees with certify's finite-difference pipeline to about 1e-5.
- The closed form rho+p_t = 2e^{2Phi} lap Phi with lap Phi = -3ma^2/(r^2+a^2)^{5/2} supports 'NEC/WEC/SEC fail at every 0<r<R_s' for m>0.

ONE ENCODING WEAKNESS, recorded:
- Check (A') is a tautology as coded. Its DEC test includes 'w<0 => not DEC' on the same sampled observers as the WEC test, so '0 bad of 234' cannot fail.

VACUITY GUARD (verify/rederive/vacuity.py):
- Dropping the p >= -rho half of the DEC: z3 finds a counterexample to DEC=>WEC (rho=0, p_i=-1/2).
- DEC => SEC: z3 finds a counterexample (rho=1/4, p_i=-1/4). So the solver is not trivially returning 'valid'.
- Dropping only the redundant rho >= 0 clause: DEC=>WEC is still valid, which is correct, because |p| <= rho already implies rho >= 0.
- The covariant check with the w clause removed: 233 tensors pass the flux-future-directed DEC and 0 fail the WEC. This is the non-tautological content (H-E: a future-directed causal flux implies the WEC), so (A')'s conclusion survives once the tautology is removed.
- Flux-causal only (FEC): 457 pass and 223 fail the WEC. So the check does discriminate when the hypothesis is weakened.
- In (C), flipping m<0 turns rho positive (+30.92). So the 'all negative' checks are not vacuous.

MINOR: the script's comments cite stale line numbers (certify.py:92-93, :94, :459). The audit JSON's own numbers (:96-97, :456) are the correct ones. This is cosmetic.

The three recorded discrepancies are confirmed as discrepancies, not refutations:
- dec_holds checks only the WEC half of the DEC.
- Sampled minima are not infima.
- The prose and selftest quote the coordinate T_00 instead of the orthonormal value, and the absolute tolerance cannot catch it.

The grade STANDS is supported.

audits.published_statement:
From MMR gr-qc/0412063 p.7-8, restating MS 1964. Metric: ds^2 = -a^2 dt^2 + b^2 dr^2 + R^2 dOmega^2, comoving. Operators: D_t = (1/a) d/dt, D_r = (1/b) d/dr, with U = D_t R and Gamma = D_r R. For p = p(e): (9) D_t U = -[Gamma/(e+p) D_r p + M/R^2 + 4 pi R p]; (12) D_r a = -a/(e+p) D_r p; (13) D_r M = 4 pi Gamma e R^2; (14) Gamma^2 = 1 + U^2 - 2M/R.

Hernandez-Misner, from MMR p.9-10: f du = a dt - b dr; (20) D_r = D_k - D_t; (25) D_k M = 4 pi R^2 [e Gamma - p U]; (26) Gamma = D_k R - U.

From HSW 0810.1083, comoving, ds^2 = -A^2dt^2 + B^2dr^2 + R^2dOmega^2:
- (14) 8 pi T_01 = -8 pi (q+eps) A B = -2(Rdot'/R - Bdot R'/(B R) - Rdot A'/(R A))
- (18) m = (R/2)[(Rdot/A)^2 - (R'/B)^2 + 1]
- (28) E = R'/B = (1 + U^2 - 2m/R)^{1/2}
- (30) D_T m = -4 pi [(P_r + eps - 4 eta sigma/3) U + (q+eps) E] R^2
- (31) D_R m = 4 pi [mu + eps + (q+eps) U/E] R^2
- (37) D_T U = -m/R^2 - 4 pi (P_r + eps - 4 eta sigma/3) R + E a

None of the sources read writes a separate D_T Gamma equation. In them that content is the tr momentum constraint, HSW eq.(14).
published_hypotheses: Spherical symmetry; four-dimensional general relativity, G_ab = 8 pi T_ab, no cosmological constant. MMR p.18 includes Lambda only by adding e_v = Lambda/8pi and p_v = -Lambda/8pi to e and p.
Diagonal metric with R the areal radius. MS uses coordinates comoving with the fluid (Lagrangian rest-mass labels, MMR eq.2-3).
MS 1964 as MMR restates it: perfect fluid with a one-parameter equation of state p = p(e).
HSW generalisation: anisotropic pressure, heat flux q, null radiation eps, shear viscosity eta, still comoving.
Hernandez-Misner: outgoing null ('observer time') slicing, perfect fluid.
For m as an integral of density: a regular centre, m(0) = 0 (HSW eq.32).
HSW: A, B, R positive; D_R = (1/R') d/dr needs R' != 0.
hypothesis_drift: BROADENED, and supported. The source works in the comoving fluid frame; the tree uses the Eulerian (slice-normal) frame with arbitrary anisotropic T and radial flux j = -T_ab u^a n^b (nonstatic.py:56-62, 66-70). An independently coded Einstein tensor gives residual 0 for all five lines (C1). They match HSW (14),(28),(30),(31),(37) with A = e^Phi, B = e^Lambda, q = j (C3, C4), and MMR (9),(12),(13),(14) at j = 0 using nabla_a T^a_r = p' + (rho+p)Phi', computed here (C5).

ADDED by the tree, and correct. EV-W (nonstatic.py:69, driven.py:238-242, foliation.py:338-341) is not a separate line in MMR or HSW. It is exactly the momentum constraint, HSW (14): the EV-W residual equals -(R e^{-Phi-Lambda}/2)(G_tr - 8 pi T_tr) (C2c, C3a). It also follows from the definition of m plus EV-U plus MS-t wherever W != 0 (C7a).

COUNTED TWICE (a discrepancy, not an error). nonstatic.py:69-70 lists EV-W and EV-U' as two equations, but their difference vanishes with no field equation used (C2a-b). They are one equation. No owner was found that relies on them being independent.

UNSTATED (nonstatic.py:297, T = G/8pi): no cosmological constant, or equivalently vacuum energy absorbed into rho and p_r. With Lambda, EV-W is unchanged (C10a). MS-r gains Lambda R^2 W/2, MS-t gains Lambda R^2 U/2, and EV-U gains Lambda R/2 with m the full MS mass (C10b-e). At the Proxima span this is 8.05e-7 M_sun against the 2.72e13 M_sun bill (N3).

UNSTATED: four-dimensional GR. With T := G/8pi the identities hold in any theory, but reading rho, p_r and j as matter needs GR. In f(R) and scalar-tensor gravity a quasi-local MS energy exists only under the integrability constraint of 0910.2387 (eq.3.7/3.13).

DROPPED at nonstatic.py:87, 'geodesic slicing (Phi = 0, always available)', also relied on at driven.py:239-241 and foliation.py:338-341. Zero shift with Phi = 0 means Gaussian normal coordinates, which exist only up to the first focal point of the normal congruence. Contracting Milne shows it: R = -t sinh chi -> 0 at t -> 0- for every chi (C9a), while W = cosh chi stays constant (C9b). So 'always available' is local only. The tree's global witnesses (C8) and the verdict SUSTAINING_FORCES_NEGATIVE_RHO = False do not move.

OVER-READING (a discrepancy). nonstatic.py:82-83 says 'The contraction variable does not know the energy density exists.' That is true of EV-W's time derivative (C1d, C7a). But rho fixes W on every slice through W^2 = 1 + U^2 - 2m/R together with MS-r (C4a, C1a).

OWNERS STATE DIFFERENT HYPOTHESES for E = R dGamma (recorded, not adjudicated). foliation.py:338-341 says it follows from choosing geodesic slicing. nonstatic.py:178-184 says '(R held fixed)', i.e. U = 0, and that zeroes U D_r Phi in any slicing (C11). At U = 0, Gamma = sqrt(1 - 2m/R) is a scalar (C12a-b; foliation.py:803 O2 states the same floor). So dGamma != 0 there needs dm != 0: dm = -R(W_f^2 - W_i^2)/2, which is -1.5R for W going from 1 to 2 (C11b). foliation.py's V13 re-slicing (foliation.py:343-347) has m = 0 and U ~ Gamma != 0. Geodesic slicing and U = 0 together force m = -4 pi R^3 p_r (C12c). This bears on BUILD_BILL_IS_GAUGE_CONDITIONAL (foliation.py:868). It is a question for the owners, and nothing is repaired.

The data claim holds. One row has a small discrepancy, which is recorded here, and none of it moves the grade.

Row by row:

(1) Numerical inputs of MS/HM/EV: "none". Correct. The rederive script feeds no number into C1-C12. The data block (N1-N3) only reproduces figures the tree computes downstream; none of them enters the equations.

(2) Lambda: the audit gave about 1.1e-52 m^-2 and marked it NAMED-NOT-READ. I have now READ it in Planck 2018 VI (1807.06209).
- Table 2, TT,TE,EE+lowE+lensing+BAO, gives H0 = 67.66 and Omega_L = 0.6889. Then 3 Omega_L H0^2/c^2 = 1.1056e-52 m^-2.
- Eq. (15) gives Lambda = 4.24e-66 eV^2, which converts to 1.089e-52 m^-2.
- With these, Lambda R^3/6 over the Proxima span is 7.97e-7 to 8.09e-7 M_sun. The audit's 8.05e-7 sits inside that range. Its ratio to the bill is Lambda R^2/6, about 3e-20.
- So "moves_conclusion: no" follows. EV-W's exact independence of Lambda (C10a) is algebra and needs no data.

(3) G = 6.67430e-11 and (4) M_sun = 1.98840e30. Both are internally consistent. GM_sun^N / G = 1.988409871e30, so 1.98841e30 is right to 6 significant figures. The bill computed from GM_sun alone, 2.720730782e13 against 2.720744289e13 (rel. -4.96e-6), reproduces in mpmath. The CODATA and IAU values were not read at source here, so they stay NAMED-NOT-READ, as the audit says. A 5e-6 change cannot move any verdict.

(5) Proxima distance. Parallax 768.0665 mas gives 4.246460 ly (reproduced); the tree uses 4.2465. The parallax was NOT found at source: I queried the Gaia EDR3 nearby-stars paper (2012.02061) and it returned no Proxima row. That value_now therefore stays "from memory, not re-read", exactly as the audit flags it. Sensitivity is linear at 6.5e-5, so "no" follows whatever the exact figure.

(6) Flat-foliation Gamma at eps = 1e-8. This row has a DISCREPANCY.
- The row says value_now 7071.067813726, "computed here (N2)".
- The tree's stated formula, 1/sqrt(1-(1-eps)^2) (foliation.py:596-599), evaluates exactly (mpmath, 40 digits) to 7071.067829543. The float stable form 1/sqrt(eps(2-eps)) gives the same.
- 7071.067813726 is a float-cancellation artifact of computing 1-(1-eps)^2 in double precision, off by a relative 2.2e-9.
- N2 compared the float formula against itself, so it reproduced the artifact rather than computing the value. The tree's own pin at foliation.py:1005-1006 carries the same artifact.
- This is a misprint-class discrepancy, not a refutation. Gamma is about 7071 either way, the bill is linear in dGamma, and nothing in rests_on_it depends on the 9th significant figure. Recorded, not repaired.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis is answered with evidence, not presumed.
- The MS/HM/EV lines are Einstein-tensor identities plus definitions, re-derived with residual 0.
- The one datum the 1964 and 1966 authors lacked, Lambda, is now READ at source. It leaves EV-W exactly unchanged and moves the other lines by about 3e-20 of the bill.
- The later literature cited (0810.1083, gr-qc/0403006, 2601.03077) extends these lines and does not correct them.
- "Not borne out for this result" is therefore supported.

The NARROWED grade rests on dropped hypotheses (local-only geodesic slicing, unstated GR and Lambda absorption), not on data, and this lens leaves it as it is.

audits.name: Electrostatic energy of the Coulomb field outside radius a, Q^2/(8 pi eps0 a), and ADM mass >= X/a

source.located: Three layers. (i) Flat-space field energy U = int_a^inf (eps0/2)E^2 dV = Q^2/(8 pi eps0 a): textbook electrostatics (Jackson, Classical Electrodynamics). Pre-arXiv, NAMED-NOT-READ. Its exact GR counterpart was READ in arXiv:2608.16534v1 (Jaraba, Campos, Baldiotti, 17 Aug 2026) p.6 eqs (38)-(39) and p.7. (ii) ADM mass of a charged thin shell: Arnowitt, Deser, Misner, PRL 4, 375 (1960) and PR 120, 313 (1960). Pre-arXiv, NAMED-NOT-READ. Restated exactly in arXiv:1303.1274v1 (R. Casadio 2013) eqs (2.22)-(2.24) and (3.1)-(3.3), using Israel's junction conditions (Israel, Nuovo Cimento B44, 1 (1966), NAMED-NOT-READ), with the areal form at eq (3.14). Also restated in arXiv:1303.2706v3 (G. Dillon 2013) Sec. 2 eq (4) and eq (9). (iii) Constants: CODATA 2022, arXiv:2409.03787v1, Tables XXXII/XXXIII p.50-51 and Table XXXVIII p.60.

audits.published_statement: 2608.16534 p.6-7: 'For an RN spacetime, the KS scalar is given by f_RN(r) = 2M/r - Q^2/r^2 ... the quasi-local energy evaluates to Delta E_RN(r) = M - Q^2/(2r)' [= the Misner-Sharp mass, eqs (31)-(33)]; 'At any finite radius r, the evaluated energy is less than the total ADM mass M. The subtracted term, -Q^2/(2r), corresponds precisely to the classical electrostatic energy of the electric field stored in the exterior region (from the boundary r to spatial infinity).' Casadio 1303.1274, restating ADM 1960 through Israel's junction equations, p.5-6: 'K_thth(r = eps) - K^0_thth(r = eps) = -m0, (2.22) leads to M^2 + 2 eps M - 2 eps m0 - Q^2 = 0, (2.23) ... M = -eps + sqrt(eps^2 + 2 eps m0 + Q^2), (2.24)'. Here eps is the isotropic radius, m0 the bare mass, M the ADM mass, and G = c = 1. Eq (3.1): as eps -> 0, M = |Q|. Eq (3.2): the areal radius is (m0 + eps + sqrt(...))/2. Eq (3.14), at areal radius lambda: 'M_lambda = m0(1 - m0/(2 lambda)) + Q^2/(2 lambda)'. Dillon 1303.2706 p.2-3, restating ADM: 'M(R) = M0 - (G/2) M(R)^2/(R c^2)' plus e^2/2R, which gives M(R -> 0) = |e|/sqrt(G).
published_hypotheses: Einstein-Maxwell theory; static and spherically symmetric; the exterior is Reissner-Nordstrom and asymptotically flat (Casadio Sec 2.2, eq 2.3)
an infinitely thin shell of bare (rest) mass m0 >= 0 and charge Q at isotropic radius eps >= 0 (eps >= r_min when |Q| > M), with a flat Minkowski interior (Casadio Sec 2.1, 2.3)

Israel junction conditions: the induced metric is continuous, and the jump in extrinsic curvature equals the shell's surface stress (Casadio eqs 2.21-2.22). The shell carries a surface tension p (eq 2.20), and the source puts no energy condition on it
geometric units G = c = 1 with Gaussian charge; the areal radius and the isotropic radius are kept distinct (Casadio eq 2.6)
the 'electrostatic energy outside r' (2608.16534 p.7) is the Misner-Sharp (quasi-local) measure M - m(r), i.e. the integral of rho over areal volume 4 pi r^2 dr, not over proper volume
flat-space version (Jackson): Coulomb field of total charge Q inside radius a, energy density eps0 E^2/2, integrated over Euclidean volume
hypothesis_drift: WEAKENED/APPROXIMATED: additivity with the bare mass. drivensource.py:360-363 (shell_ratio: 'BARE mass mu. Equals 1/(1 + mu a / X)') and :427 (z3 model 'Mt == mu + X / a') add the flat-space field energy to the bare mass. In exact GR the bare rest mass enters as M = m0 + Q^2/2a - m0^2/2a (Casadio eq 3.14; re-derived here in section D), so the tree drops the gravitational binding term -G m0^2/(2 a c^2). The additive form becomes exact if mu is read as the Misner-Sharp mass at the surface, m(a+) = M - X/a, which is how :149 words it ('the body's own contribution to M'). The conclusion is unaffected: z3 proves r_c <= a for every GR shell with m0 >= 0. At the pinned configuration (:550) the correction is 3.7e-28 kg. This is a discrepancy in the model, not a refutation.

IMPLICIT: which volume measure. drivensource.py:144-145 ('carries energy Q^2/(8 pi eps0 a)') uses the flat-space formula. In GR this value is exact only as the areal integral, which equals M - m(a) = X/a. The proper-volume integral is strictly larger (0.1654 vs 0.1350 at M = 1, Q = 0.9, a = 3). The bound uses only M - m(a), so the drift is harmless.

UNSTATED: the supremum needs exotic matter. drivensource.py:157-159 and :552 put r_c = a exactly at zero bare mass. For a static shell with m0 = 0, sigma = 0 and the Israel junction gives p = -Q^2/(16 pi a^3) < 0 (section G). So sigma + p < 0 and the NEC fails on the shell. The supremum is reached only by NEC-violating shell matter, and under the NEC the bound is strict. The tree does not claim the supremum is physical, so this is recorded, not charged against it.

SCOPED: the interior step. drivensource.py:162-164 (regular centre + rho >= 0 => m >= 0) holds on a static slice, since G^t_t = -2m'/r^2 (section H). On a non-static slice the tree's own identity D_r m = 4 pi R^2 (rho W + j U) (drivensource.py:339) means rho >= 0 is not enough; Hayward Prop 6 needs the DEC and an untrapped slice. drivensource.EM_CLOSED_BY (line 456) places section 4 on the 'static branch', so the tree's use falls inside the valid class. The canonical hypothesis list does not state staticity; this entry names it.

SCOPE TENSION, named here and not a drift of the external result: drivensource.SCOPE (lines 459-460) says 'pure electrovac ... Charged fluids ... are not measured', but the body of radius a is necessarily non-electrovac matter. The bound is covered without any fluid model: it needs only M = m(a) + X/a (exact for an RN exterior) and m(a) >= 0.
NO DRIFT on units: X = Q^2/(8 pi eps0 c^2) and r_c = X/M are exact in SI, with G cancelling (drivensource.py:348-357).

rederivation.outcome: 33 PASS, 0 FAIL (exit 0, ~1.6 s; md5 80bbc20da52bcd633e2fe23211fdbf64). sympy checks: the flat Coulomb energy outside a is Q^2/(8 pi eps0 a). The RN Misner-Sharp mass in SI is M - X/r with G cancelling, and r_c = X/M. In GR the areal integral of rho is exactly X/a, and the proper-volume integral is larger. The Israel static shell gives M = m0 + Q^2/2a - m0^2/2a (Casadio 3.14). The ADM quadratic (Casadio 2.23) equals the Israel relation identically under a = eps + (m0+M)/2. As eps -> 0, M -> |Q| at areal radius (m0+|Q|)/2 >= r_c. G^t_t = -2m'/r^2. At m0 = 0 the shell has p = -Q^2/(16 pi a^3) < 0, so the NEC fails on the shell. z3 checks (vacuity and drift guards sat): the tree's E2 is re-proved on the tree's own model. For a GR shell, m0 in [0,2a] => 2Ma >= Q^2, strictly for m0 in (0,2a). For an ADM shell with eps >= 0 and m0 >= 0, m0 <= 2a follows automatically and 2Ma >= Q^2. For a general body with M = m(a) + Q^2/2a and m(a) >= 0, r_c <= a. Numerically, the tree's X per C^2 and its pin 0.4999847997 are reproduced under both CODATA 2018 and CODATA 2022. Dillon's eq (27) model lies below e^2/2R for every R.

later_literature.what: Re-derives ADM 1960 from Israel's junction equations. Every static shell with m0 >= 0 obeys M >= Q^2/(2 a_areal) (proved by z3 here), so the tree's bound holds in exact GR, including the binding term the tree's weak-field formula drops. The eps -> 0 limit gives finite M = |Q| at areal radius (m0+|Q|)/2 > 0, so it is not an areal point charge. That is consistent with specthm V6 keeping the RN point charge outside the hypothesis.

Restates ADM, then proposes a Newtonian 'additive' renormalisation (eqs 25-27) in which M_e(R) < e^2/(2Rc^2). In that model r_c would lie outside the shell. The model is Newtonian with an extra assumption and does not solve the Einstein-Maxwell junction problem; exact GR gives M = Q^2/2a at m0 = 0. It is recorded as a contested model, not as evidence against the tree.

The quasi-local energy of RN equals the Misner-Sharp mass M - Q^2/2r, and the subtracted term is 'precisely' the exterior electrostatic energy. This gives the exact GR meaning of drivensource.py:144-145.

audits.lacked_data: Tested against M's hypothesis. (1) The exterior energy Q^2/(8 pi eps0 a) is a closed-form integral whose only datum is eps0. Before the 2019 SI revision eps0 was exact; it is now measured, and CODATA 2022 moved it by 6.8e-10 relative. Computed: X and the pinned r_c/a move by less than 2e-10, and no value of eps0 can reverse the inequality r_c <= a. (2) The ADM/Israel shell mass is an Einstein-Maxwell theorem and uses no measured datum; G cancels from X and r_c. What the flat-space picture lacks is a term, not data: it omits gravitational binding, and so does drivensource.py's model at :360 and :427. The exact GR relation includes binding and still gives M >= Q^2/2a, which z3 proves here. Evidence against the hypothesis for this result: no datum that has moved, or could move, changes the conclusion. Evidence for a weaker form of it: flat additivity is incomplete in strong fields, and the Newtonian alternative in Dillon 2013 even disagrees on which way the effect goes, but that incompleteness does not reach the bound.
audits.grade_evidence: The published statements (2608.16534 p.7; Casadio eqs 2.23-2.24 and 3.14) are re-derived exactly, 33/33 checks passing. The tree's conclusion r_c <= a is machine-checked in exact GR, not only on the tree's flat model. z3 proves 2Ma >= Q^2 for every ADM shell with eps >= 0 and m0 >= 0, and for any body with M = m(a) + Q^2/2a and m(a) >= 0; the guards are sat. The interior step holds on a static slice, which is where drivensource.py:456 places section 4. The only datum that moved (eps0, CODATA 2022) shifts the pin by 1.7e-10, inside its tolerance. Three discrepancies are recorded, and none is a refutation. First, shell_ratio (:360-363, :427) is the weak-field form; it is exact if mu is read as the surface Misner-Sharp mass, as :149 words it. Second, the supremum (:157-159) is reached only by an NEC-violating shell. Third, staticity of the interior step is implicit. The grade is not NARROWED, because in exact GR the bound holds on every configuration with non-negative bare mass, the whole class the tree uses.
audits.what_would_change_the_grade: NARROWED if the tree applied the bound to a non-static charged body (that needs the DEC and an untrapped slice), or quoted 1/(1 + mu a/X) as exact for strong-field shells. WRONG only if some static Einstein-Maxwell body with a regular centre, or a thin shell with m0 >= 0, had an RN exterior with M < X/a. The z3 proofs here exclude that within those models, so a counterexample would need a non-RN exterior (nonlinear electrodynamics, non-spherical fields, or Lambda), all outside drivensource.SCOPE. Reading ADM 1960 or Israel 1966 at source and finding a different junction relation would reopen sections D and E.

verifiers.lens: REFUTE THE GRADE (either direction) for coulomb-exterior-field-energy, graded STANDS
verifiers.reason:
I tried to refute the grade in both directions and could not. STANDS holds.

What I read at source through alphaXiv:
- Casadio arXiv:1303.1274v1, full text. Eqs (2.22)-(2.24), (2.6), (3.1)-(3.3) and (3.14) match the audit's quotes word for word: K_thth - K0_thth = -m0; M^2 + 2 eps M - 2 eps m0 - Q^2 = 0; M = -eps + sqrt(eps^2 + 2 eps m0 + Q^2); areal radius (m0 + |Q|)/2 as eps -> 0; M_lambda = m0(1 - m0/2 lambda) + Q^2/2 lambda.
- Jaraba-Campos-Baldiotti arXiv:2608.16534v1, pp. 6-7, eqs (31)-(33) and (38)-(39). Delta E_RN = M - Q^2/2r. The p.7 quote that the subtracted term 'corresponds precisely to the classical electrostatic energy ... stored in the exterior region' is verbatim.
- CODATA 2022 arXiv:2409.03787v1. Table XXXIII gives eps0 = 8.854 187 8188(14)e-12 and G = 6.674 30(15)e-11 (unchanged, p.47 and p.60). Table XXXVIII gives eps0 D_r = +4.5. With rounded values I first got 4.6, but the source states 4.5 computed with extra digits, so the audit's '+4.5 sigma' is right.

What I checked independently:
- The auditor's script re-runs to 33 PASS, 0 FAIL, md5 80bbc20d... as stated.
- drivensource.py md5 is 5c67a71c9750390fbc83a03de745b236 as stated, and its own --selftest shows the pin 0.4999847997 ok.
- With mpmath: the proper-volume integral is 0.165410 against the areal 0.135. X per C^2 is 5.00000000272e-8 under CODATA 2018 and 4.99999999933e-8 under CODATA 2022. The 4472 C, 1 m, 1 kg ratio r_c/a is 0.499984799674 under 2018 and 0.499984799505 under 2022, which is 1.95e-10 from the pin, inside its 1e-9 tolerance.
- Israel static shell by hand: sqrt(f) = 1 - m0/a gives M = m0 + Q^2/2a - m0^2/2a. Correct.

The one possible hole I found, and why it does not change the grade:
- Casadio's (2.22) as written is the unsquared relation sqrt(f) = 1 - m0/a, which needs m0 <= a. At small eps with m0 > |Q|, the ADM solution has areal a = (m0 + |Q|)/2 < m0. So it lies on the branch where the sign of K flips (Casadio's own 'worm-holes' remark, p.7). The audit's z3 proofs work with the squared relation, which covers both branches.
- I checked in sympy that a - m0/2 = eps + M/2 >= 0 identically, so M - Q^2/2a = m0(1 - m0/2a) >= 0 on both branches. Sample: m0 = 3, Q = 1, eps = 1e-3 gives 1 - m0/a = -0.50 and a bound margin of +0.75.
- On the flipped branch the slice passes a throat at R+ >= M >= |Q| >= Q^2/2M = r_c, so no negative-m region appears outside the shell either.
- A static shell with m0 > 2a needs a < r_c inside r-, with an exterior containing r = 0. That exterior is not asymptotically flat. The exclusion is therefore physical, not an artefact of the parametrisation.

Downstream uses:
- specthm R3 and the 'electrovac' hypothesis use the bound only under non-negative bare mass, rho >= 0 and a regular centre.
- V6 keeps the point charge out of the hypothesis, which agrees with Casadio's eps -> 0 limit being of finite areal size.
- None of these applies the bound to a non-static body, and EM_CLOSED_BY says 'static branch'.

The three recorded discrepancies are correctly kept as discrepancies, not refutations, with nothing charged in M's favour: weak-field additivity at :360/:427, the NEC-violating supremum, and the implicit staticity. The only moved datum (eps0) cannot reverse an inequality.

One minor wording point, not affecting the grade: the 'areal form' the audit cites as eq (3.14) is Casadio's lambda-cutoff evaluation. It holds at any areal radius only because (3.13)-(3.14) are a reparametrisation of (2.24) through (3.2), which the audit's section E re-derives.

ADM 1960 and Israel 1966 stay NAMED-NOT-READ. They are read only through the restatements, as the audit itself states. I edited nothing under research/ (git status is clean).

verifiers.lens: RE-RUN THE RE-DERIVATION: run the audit's script from a copy in my own directory, check that its encoding matches the published statement, and run vacuity guards with the hypotheses negated.
verifiers.reason:
Re-run: I copied the script to verify/rederive/. Its md5 is 80bbc20da52bcd633e2fe23211fdbf64, the same as the audit's. It gives 33 PASS, 0 FAIL, exit 0. drivensource.py md5 is 5c67a71c9750390fbc83a03de745b236, also as claimed. I re-read the owner lines 140-164, 348-363, 420-433, 452-460 and 535-552, and the statements match the canonical entry.

Encoding against source: I read Casadio 1303.1274 at source through alphaXiv (full paper, pp.1-11). The script's equations match it exactly: eq (2.6) the isotropic-to-areal map, (2.23) the ADM quadratic, (2.24), (3.2), (3.3) the areal radius (m0+|Q|)/2, and (3.14) M = m0 + (Q^2 - m0^2)/(2 lambda). Section D's Israel solve reproduces (3.14). Section E's identity Israel(a = eps + (m0+M)/2) == (2.23) holds term by term. So the script checks the theorem, not a toy of it. The tree's own E2, run on the flat additive model, is re-run exactly as drivensource.py:426-433 writes it.

Vacuity guards: I wrote my own script, vacuity_coulomb.py, using z3 and mpmath. Negating each hypothesis gives a concrete counterexample, so none of the proofs is vacuous:
- m(a) < 0 on the general body gives a counterexample.
- eps < 0 on the ADM shell gives one (Q=1, m0=1, M=1, eps=-3/4).
- m0 < 0 with eps >= 0 gives one (M=0, Q=2).
- With all hypotheses kept, the negated conclusion is unsat.
- The proper-volume integral is 0.165410463603 by mpmath, against the areal value 0.135, matching the script's quadrature.
- I encoded the NEC on the shell as sigma + p >= 0, using the Israel surface pressure on the sqrt(f) > 0 branch. With 2Ma = Q^2 this is unsat, which confirms 'under the NEC the bound is strict'. The guard is sat.

One encoding refinement, not a refutation. Section D solves the SQUARED junction relation f_out = (1 - m0/a)^2, which merges the two sign branches of sqrt(f_out). The z3 Israel proof then assumes m0 <= 2a rather than deriving it.
- On the other branch, 1 + s = m0/a, with m0 > 2a, my z3 run finds a counterexample to 2Ma >= Q^2: Q=2, a=1, m0=3, M=1/2.
- That configuration has |Q| > M and no throat. Its 'exterior' runs inward to the naked singularity, so it is not asymptotically flat, and the audit's first named hypothesis excludes it.
- On the outward-normal branch (1 - s = m0/a, s >= 0), the bound is unsat to violate, so it holds outright. That branch forces m0 <= a.
- The ADM parametrisation proves m0 <= 2a for every eps >= 0 and m0 >= 0. That covers Casadio's wormhole-side shells (a < m0 <= 2a, through the throat), and the bound holds there too.

So the audit's wording 'every GR shell with m0 >= 0' holds only together with the stated hypothesis that the exterior is asymptotically flat. The record should keep that hypothesis named and not drop it.

Minor: check J, the Dillon model, is weakly encoded. It tests a derivative identity plus a single point. The inequality it stands for, 1 - e^-x < x for x > 0, is true, and nothing rests on J.

Data: the CODATA 2018 and 2022 values of eps0 both reproduce X per C^2 ≈ 5e-8 and the pin 0.4999847997 within the tree's 1e-9 tolerance. The GR binding term is 3.7e-28 kg.

Conclusion: the evidence supports STANDS, under the named hypotheses (Einstein-Maxwell theory, static, spherical, asymptotically flat RN exterior, m(a) >= 0 or bare mass m0 >= 0). The three recorded discrepancies in the tree are the weak-field additivity, the supremum needing an NEC-violating shell, and implicit staticity. They are correctly graded as discrepancies, not refutations.

audits.published_statement: 0804.2182 p.6: 'Our version of the Bekenstein bound then reads S_V <= K_V, which is S(rho_V) - S(rho^0_V) <= tr(K rho_V) - tr(K rho^0_V) (17) ... we can write (17) simply as tr(rho_V log rho_V) - tr(rho_V log rho^0_V) >= 0 (18). This is just the statement of the positivity of the relative entropy ... It is always positive (20), and is zero only when rho1 = rho2. This gives a proof of the present formulation of the bound.' 1309.1121 p.2: 'Delta S_A <= Delta<H_A> (3) ... In the form (3), the bound is valid for any region A (not necessarily the half space) and for any "object" state rho^1, due to the positivity of relative entropy S(rho^1_A|rho^0_A) = Delta<H_A> - Delta S_A >= 0 (4)'. Also on p.2: 'Eq. (3) allows ... for negative values on both sides of the inequality ... negative energy in A must be accompanied by a decrease of the entanglement entropy'.
published_hypotheses: H1: V (= A) is a spatial region on a Cauchy surface, with algebra A(V) of its causal development (0804.2182 p.2).
H2: the reference state is the global vacuum. rho^0_V = tr_{-V}|0><0| and K = H_A = -log rho^0_V up to a constant, the vacuum modular Hamiltonian (p.3-4 eq.6; PRL p.1).

H3: a cutoff (lattice) regularisation with H = H_V (x) H_{-V}. The continuum statement goes through Araki's relative entropy, while separate continuum definitions of S_V and K_V 'have not been worked out' (footnote 2, p.6).
H4: the object state has acceptable UV behaviour, e.g. finite energy, so the divergences cancel in S_V and K_V (p.3, p.5-6).
H5: fixed background geometry. The relative entropy 'becomes ill defined once the backreaction is included' (p.8).
H6: the form S <= 2 pi E R is recovered only for a half space (Bisognano-Wichmann, eq.7) far from the boundary, or for a sphere in a CFT (eq.9). For general regions or theories K is non-local (p.4).
H7: flat space. The black-hole version, eqs 15 and 28, uses K = 8 pi G M E, where G does enter.
hypothesis_drift: NOTATION, a discrepancy and not a refutation (bounds.py:162, bounds.py:307). The tree writes 'dS_A <= d<H_A>'. Both sources write finite differences, Delta S_A <= Delta<H_A>, between the object state and the vacuum (0804.2182 eq.17; 1309.1121 eq.3). Read as differentials it would be the first law, an equality at first order (rederive B). Every use in the tree treats it as the finite-difference bound, so no conclusion moves.
DROPPED, harmless for this use: H2, the vacuum reference state (bounds.py:162-166 says only 'modular energy'). The member's cell does not depend on it.

DROPPED, harmless for this use, and named here: H5, the fixed background (0804.2182 p.8). It is an unseated candidate Z = 2 member with an energy-density integrand; recorded, not adjudicated. Its ref [10], Borde-Ford-Roman gr-qc/0109061, is NAMED-NOT-READ.

later_literature.what: Rigorous proof of 'Casini's version of the Bekenstein bound' (eq.8, Thm III.1) with Delta S defined independently through a crossed-product regulator. Assumes a globally KMS reference state, cyclic-separating object states, an existing stress tensor and finite relative entropy. Extends to bifurcate Killing horizons.
A complementary, rigorous, model-independent upper bound: S(phi||omega) <= 2 pi R E(phi;B) for states localised in a region of width 2R. Cites Longo & Xu, arXiv:1802.07184, which is NAMED-NOT-READ.

Narrows the interpretation only: the formulation is 'widely accepted proven' but 'not the only viable', and the reading as an information limit is 'folklore'. The inequality and the tree's coding are untouched.

audits.lacked_data: What the 2008 author lacked was mathematical, not empirical. Footnote 2 says separate continuum definitions of Delta S_V and Delta K_V 'have not been worked out'; the inequality itself was already a theorem through Araki's relative entropy. Those definitions were supplied in 2023 (arXiv:2312.07646 Thm III.1) under named hypotheses, and the bound came out exactly as stated. That is evidence for the result. No measured datum enters the conclusion, and the only constant, 2 pi, is exact and unused by the inequality. The one limitation later work does not remove is H5, the fixed background (p.8). It is a named hypothesis, not missing data, and the tree does not use the bound beyond it. For this result M's hypothesis was tested and is not supported: the later data confirm the conclusion rather than change it.

The re-derivation agrees. A later rigorous proof (2312.07646) confirms it, and no datum is involved. The four withdrawals that rest on it (bounds.py:174-182, 463-474) are recomputed and hold. Recorded without changing the grade: (i) the tree writes d where the sources write Delta; (ii) K = 1 conflicts with the source's equality condition and with its asymptotic saturation (43)-(44). This is a coding discrepancy for the tree to rule on: recoding moves E(statistics) from 1 to 3 and the saturated-count pin from 4 to 5, and no conclusion. (iii) bounds.py:261-264 needs 'state-independent RHS' named as a hypothesis. (iv) bounds.py:166-167 'E = 2' is stale; it is E = 1 now, a tree-internal figure.

audits.published_statement:
arXiv:2510.20843 p.5: 'Let f : [a,b] -> R be an absolutely continuous function. Then: 1. f is differentiable almost everywhere on [a,b], 2. its derivative f' is Lebesgue integrable on [a,b], and 3. for all x in [a,b], f(x) = f(a) + INT_a^x f'(t) dt. Conversely, if g in L^1([a,b]) and we define F(x) = INT_a^x g(t) dt, then F is absolutely continuous on [a,b], F' = g almost everywhere.'

p.1: 'a function F defined on [a,b] is absolutely continuous if and only if F' exists almost everywhere, belongs to L^1([a,b]), and F(x) = F(a) + INT_a^x F'(t) dt.'

p.2, Def 2.0.1: AC on an interval I is the eps-delta condition over finite disjoint subintervals of I. p.2: 'A function may be absolutely continuous on every compact subinterval yet fail to be absolutely continuous globally.'

arXiv:2403.18229 p.13: 'for f in L^1, F(x) := INT_{]-oo,x]} f(t) dmu is differentiable and F'(x) = f(x) a.e.'
published_hypotheses: Compact interval [a,b] (2510.20843 p.5). On a non-compact interval only AC on each compact subinterval (AC_loc) comes for free, and AC_loc does not imply AC (p.2, Example 3.0.1).
F is absolutely continuous on [a,b] in the eps-delta sense of Def 2.0.1 (p.2).
The conclusion is an identity between LEBESGUE integrals: F' exists a.e. and lies in L^1([a,b]) (p.5).
The theorem makes no assumption about the value of F at the endpoint. F(a) appears in the conclusion, so the FTC never sets a boundary term to zero.

Continuity plus a.e. differentiability is not enough: the theorem is an iff, and the Cantor function is the standard counterexample. That counterexample is re-derived here (T4); 2510.20843 does not show it.
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED: 'the limit is ZERO'. tolman.py:935 words the hypothesis as 'r^3 p_r must be absolutely continuous on (0, R] with a limit at 0', and :935-936 says 'Regular centre means exactly that'. With a limit L at 0, the FTC gives m(R) = 4 pi (R^3 p_r(R) - L) (T1). The conclusion at :933-934, m = 4 pi R^3 p_r, needs L = 0. The tree's own independence_witness (tolman.py:1380-1386, V32 at :1937) meets the hypothesis exactly as worded: r^3 p_r = A is constant, so it is AC on (0,R] with limit A. Yet the identity fails by -4 pi A (T2). The zero limit IS carried elsewhere in the same file: :51 says 'r^3 p_r -> 0', the master formula at :281-286 carries C = 4 pi lim r^3 p_r, and z3's FULL at :2055 imposes Cc == 0 before B1 (:2070) is discharged. The drift is confined to the citing sentence.

OVERSTATED COMPARISON: tolman.py:936 says the regular centre 'is STRONGER than p_r is finite at the centre'. Read as an implication, this fails. The tree's own W3 (tolman.py:584, p_r = -2 + 10 r^(-5/2), labelled 'regular centre') has r^3 p_r -> 0 while p_r -> +oo (T3). The true half is the other direction: finiteness alone does not suffice (Cantor witness, T4). The two conditions are incomparable, not ordered. This is a wording discrepancy, not a refutation of anything the file computes.

WEAKENED/AMBIGUOUS: 'absolutely continuous on (0, R]' (tolman.py:935) is stated on a half-open interval, and it can be read two ways. (a) AC on (0,R] itself, in Def 2.0.1's sense: this implies uniform continuity, so the limit at 0 exists automatically ('with a limit at 0' is then redundant) and r^2 u is in L^1(0,R). (b) AC_loc, i.e. AC on every compact subinterval: then the FTC plus the limit gives the identity with m(R) as an IMPROPER integral, which need not be a Lebesgue integral. Example: r^3 p_r = r^2 sin(r^-2) is differentiable on (0,R] with limit 0, while INT |r^2 u| diverges logarithmically (T6). The tree does not say which reading it means; m is written INT_0^R r^2 u dr. Where u has one sign (the G2 route, :940-942), monotone convergence makes the two readings agree.

ADDED (a hypothesis the tree may not need): if the ODE d/dr(r^3 p_r) = r^2 u holds at EVERY r in (0,R], which is the pointwise setting of V2/V3, then F = m - 4 pi r^3 p_r has F' = 0 identically (T5). F is then constant by the mean-value theorem, with no absolute-continuity hypothesis at all. The same file's own device, 'C IS A FIRST INTEGRAL, NOT A LIMIT' (:291-296), takes exactly this route. AC is load-bearing only when the ODE holds merely almost everywhere (T4). So the hypothesis is sufficient but not necessary. Recorded, not a fault.

audits.lacked_data: M's hypothesis, tested on this result. The 2010-2013 MuLan authors lacked three things: (i) the O(alpha^3) QED correction and a modern dispersive hadronic term (they carried a 0.14 ppm theory uncertainty from 'unknown 3-loop'); (ii) the CODATA 2018/2022 muon mass (105.6583755 vs 105.6583715 MeV) and the exact hbar; (iii) later lifetime data in the average (2196981.1 vs 2196980.3 ps). All three have since arrived. Eberhart et al. 2026 computed (i) and used (ii)-(iii), obtaining 1.16637859(59)e-5. That is 0.18 ppm (0.36 sigma) below the tree's pin, a move of 9.0e-8 in v and 1.8e-7 in rho_EW (COMPUTED). For this result the evidence runs AGAINST the hypothesis: having the data did not change the conclusion. Data is still lacking in one place: an independent G_F at muon-decay precision. The EW-fit and CKM routes are about 1000x less precise and disagree with G_mu by +2 and -3 sigma (2102.02825), so whether G_mu carries a BSM admixture of order 1e-3 is OPEN. Even a full 1e-3 admixture would move v by at most 3.8e-4, which cannot move any order-of-magnitude figure. For the TREE RELATION, what is missing is a hypothesis rather than data. The tree uses LO lambda and V_min, although the loop-level parameters were available (Buttazzo 2013, before the tree was written); they move lambda by -2.4 % and m^2 by +10.5 %.

audits.name: Closed form of modified spherical Bessel functions of the second kind k_l(x) = e^{-x} sum_j (l+j)!/(j!(l-j)!) (2x)^{-j} / x

source.located: Classical special-function identity. The standard references are DLMF 10.47.9 (k_n = sqrt(pi/(2z)) K_{n+1/2}), DLMF 10.49.12 (k_n(z) = (pi/2) e^{-z} sum_{k=0}^n (n+k)!/(2^k k!(n-k)!) z^{-k-1}) and Abramowitz & Stegun 10.2.15. None of these is on arXiv, so they are NAMED-NOT-READ. The closed form is READ through an exact restatement in arXiv:2207.00707v4 (Stoutemyer 2022), Sec. 5, pp.22-23: Table 6 rows n=0..4, recurrence (17), the Rayleigh-type formula, k_n ~ e^{-x}/x, and the note that DLMF defines k_n as pi/2 times the table's normalisation. The radial ODE and the 3D exterior multipole expansion are READ in arXiv:2003.03370v1 (Hinzen et al. 2020): eqs (14), (39) and (41).
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 2207.00707 (pp.1,3,5-8,12-14,17-20,22-29) and 2003.03370 (pp.1-6,8-9). DLMF and A&S were read only through Stoutemyer's restatement. The closed form for all l is also re-derived here from the ODE (check C1). The owner was re-read in the working tree: research/warp-drive/excite.py, md5 a866f2f7745baca63aad910aeeb20a69, commit 524ccae, lines 66-83, 101, 708-743, 1075-1082, 1201-1204, 1490-1497 and 1767-1776.

published_hypotheses: l is a non-negative integer. The sum terminates only for half-integer order l+1/2.
z != 0. There is a pole of order l+1 at the origin.
Normalisation: MathWorld/Stoutemyer write k_n = e^{-x} q_n(x). DLMF's k_n is pi/2 times that, which equals sqrt(pi/(2z)) K_{n+1/2}(z).
The ODE is the 3-dimensional radial modified Helmholtz equation, with angular eigenvalue l(l+1). k_l is the solution that decays at infinity.
Multipole use (2003.03370): a LINEAR equation, with the source compactly supported inside a sphere, and the expansion valid outside it. It runs over all l; l_max is only a numerical cutoff.
hypothesis_drift: No drift on the identity itself. The tree's p_l(y) (excite.py:710-712, 715-719) is exactly the MathWorld/Stoutemyer normalisation: Table 6 is reproduced coefficient by coefficient (C4). It is also (2/pi) times DLMF 10.49.12, agreeing with K_{l+1/2} to 2.3e-41 (C3). The tree's 'up to normalisation' is accurate.

RESTRICTED, not dropped (excite.py:79, 1490-1492, 1767-1776). The tree checks only l = 0..5, while the source covers every integer l >= 0. This audit proves the identity for general l symbolically (C1) and checks it exactly for l <= 12 (C2). A general non-spherical tail needs every l, so the l > 5 content that 'covered ... by the multipole witnesses k_l (l = 0..5)' relies on is supplied by the source and by C1, not by the tree's own check.

UNNAMED in the tree (excite.py:77-79, 1082). H-e says the nonlinear proof is radial 'in any dimension d', but the multipole witnesses k_l with eigenvalue l(l+1) solve the radial equation only in d = 3. C8a shows the tree's k_l fails f'' + (d-1)f'/x - l(l+d-2)f/x^2 - f = 0 for d = 2, 4, 5. The d-dimensional analogue x^{1-d/2} K_{l+d/2-1} does solve it, and its rate still tends to 1 (C8b), but the tree does not seat it. So non-spherical coverage carries an unnamed hypothesis: d = 3.

ADDED by the tree and named ('linear tail (f small)', excite.py:78-79). The linear coefficient of (1/2)f(f+1)(f+2) is exactly 1 (C7), so the operator matches the source's (Delta - 1). But neither the source (which is linear) nor any tree row for l >= 1 proves that the nonlinear O(f^2) remainder leaves the non-spherical tail rate unchanged. The tree's nonlinear proof, steps (i)-(iii), is radial only.

IMPLICIT (excite.py:78-79). Carrying 'rate -> 1' through an infinite sum over l means swapping a limit and a series, and neither the tree nor the source restatement says so. The step is supplied here (C9): k_l(x) e^x x = 1 + positive powers of 1/x, decreasing in x, so for x >= X > r_s each term is bounded by its value at X and the per-l limit passes to the sum.

As printed it reads q_n = q_{n-1} + (2n-1)/x q_{n-2}, and that is false: the residual at n=2 is -(x-3)/x^3, and it is nonzero for n=2..6. audits.name: The hierarchy problem: v sits sixteen orders below the (reduced) Planck scale

source.located: There is no single originating paper. The 'hierarchy problem' is a statement the field built up over time: Gildener-Weinberg 1976, Wilson 1970, Susskind 1978, 't Hooft 1979 and Veltman 1981, all NAMED-NOT-READ. It was READ at source in three standard restatements: G.F. Giudice, 'Naturally Speaking', arXiv:0801.2562v2 (2008), secs 2-5 and 9, eqs (1), (5), (9); N. Craig, 'Naturalness: A Snowmass White Paper', arXiv:2205.05708v1 (2022), sec 5; S. Koren, 'The Hierarchy Problem: From the Fundamentals to the Frontiers', arXiv:2009.11870v1 (2020), ch.2. The threshold the tree equates it with is Barcelo & Visser, gr-qc/0003025v2: eq (2.1) p.3, ANEC cases 1-3 p.6, and the m_p/sqrt(xi) sentence on p.16. Data sources: CODATA 2022, arXiv:2409.03787 (Tables XXX, XXXII, XXXIII), and MuLan, arXiv:1211.0960 eq (24).
source.via: Read with alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 0801.2562, 2205.05708, 2009.11870, gr-qc/0003025, 2409.03787 and 1211.0960; the returned page text is quoted in the report. The original 1970s-80s papers are NAMED-NOT-READ. The statement audited is the one the three reviews give, and the three agree with each other.

audits.published_statement: Giudice 0801.2562 sec 2: 'the ratio between the Fermi constant G_F and the Newton constant G_N ... is a very large number G_F hbar^2/(G_N c^2) = 1.738 59(15) x 10^33 (1)' [PDG 2006]. Sec 3: 'The really problematic aspect about the G_F/G_N ratio in eq. (1) comes about when we consider the effects of quantum mechanics', with delta m_H^2 = kappa Lambda^2 (5), and 'if we take Lambda = M_Pl [= G_N^{-1/2}], the cancellation in kappa must be one part in 10^32.' Craig 2205.05708 sec 5: 'The Standard Model in isolation does not suffer from a hierarchy problem ... It is only in the presence of additional UV scales that the problem emerges ... it is typical to invoke Lambda ~ M_Pl ... quantum corrections that are 32 orders of magnitude in excess of the doublet mass parameter.' Koren 2009.11870 sec 2.3: 'In a theory of physics beyond the Standard Model where the Higgs mass is an output, physical parameters must be finely-tuned in order to produce a mass which is far below the scale of new physics.' Also sec 2.2.1: 'There is no hierarchy problem in the Standard Model.'
published_hypotheses: H1 (the datum): the measured ratio of the weak scale to the gravitational scale is G_F/G_N ~ 1.7e33, i.e. v << M_Pl. This is a measurement, not the problem.

H2 (the problem proper): the Higgs mass is an OUTPUT of a more fundamental theory whose physical scales above the weak scale (GUT, Planck, Landau pole) couple to the Higgs. Then delta m_H^2 ~ Lambda^2, and m_H << Lambda needs a fine-tuned cancellation (Giudice secs 3-4; Craig sec 5; Koren sec 2.3).
H3: no symmetry of the SM protects a scalar mass (technical naturalness; Giudice sec 4; Koren sec 1.3).

audits.published_statement: Note [18] (pp. 8-9): 'The connection begins with the observation that the following three statements are equivalent, where A is a self-adjoint operator (with domain D(A) and spectrum sigma(A)) representing a quantum observable: (a) <psi | A psi> >= -Q for all normalised psi in D(A); (b) sigma(A) subset [-Q, oo); (c) the probability measure mu_psi that describes the distribution of individual measurement results of A in state psi has support supp mu_psi subset [-Q, oo). [The implication (a) => (b) is the Rayleigh-Ritz variational principle; (b) => (c) because measurements always give values in the spectrum; (c) => (a) because any random variable taking values in [-Q, oo) has its expected value in that range.] In general, supp mu_psi (for a fixed choice of psi) can be a proper subset of sigma(A), and in particular the infimum of the support of mu_psi can exceed inf sigma(A). ... However, the spectrum and the support of the probability measure coincide if A is a local observable, such as a smeared field, and psi is the vacuum state Omega of a Minkowski space QFT obeying the standard assumptions of algebraic quantum field theory [11]. ... In particular, sigma(A) and supp mu_Omega have a common infimum, which provides a sharp quantum inequality bound <psi | A psi> >= inf supp mu_Omega for all normalized psi in D(A).' Body, p. 2: 'These lower bounds represent the lowest eigenvalues of the smeared operators. As a consequence of the Reeh-Schlieder theorem ..., they are also the lower bounds of the support of the corresponding probability distributions in the vacuum state [18].'
published_hypotheses: N1: A is SELF-ADJOINT. A symmetric operator on a dense domain is not enough. D(A) is the domain of that self-adjoint operator.
N2: (a) holds for ALL normalised psi in D(A), i.e. one state-independent bound Q over the whole domain of that self-adjoint operator.
N3: mu_psi is the spectral measure <psi, P_A(.) psi>, the Born-rule distribution of individual outcomes. 'Distribution' means the quantum spectral measure.
N4: the three-way equivalence is abstract Hilbert-space operator theory. It assumes no spacetime, dimension, field or state.
N5: (c) for ONE fixed psi does not give (b). The equivalence is with (c) for every psi; the note's own caveat is that inf supp mu_psi can exceed inf sigma(A).
N6: spectrum = support, and hence a sharp bound, holds ONLY for local A and psi the vacuum of a MINKOWSKI QFT obeying the AQFT axioms (Reeh-Schlieder).

N7: Q can be any valid bound. Only the OPTIMAL Q equals inf sigma(A). The body sentence 'these lower bounds represent the lowest eigenvalues' is exact only for optimal bounds: FFR 1204.3570 p. 12 shows the Fewster-Eveson 4D bound is about 9x weaker than the estimated optimal one.
hypothesis_drift: NONE in the flat theorem C1 (noise.py:165-177). N1 is supplied by H3 (noise.py:156-162): A_tau is the Friedrichs extension on Hadamard vectors, which is the self-adjoint operator FFR 1204.3570 p. 2 say they mean. N2 is met because the tree bounds the FORM on the form domain (noise.py:172-173). That domain contains D(A), so the premise is stronger, not weaker. N3 is H6 word for word (noise.py:164-168). Only (a)=>(b)=>(c) is used, never N6. The chain is used exactly as published.

WEAKENED (the domain and self-adjoint-realisation hypothesis, N1+N2) in the CURVED application. noise.py:42-44 and ledger.py:1822-1826 (the O2 row; LEDGER.md:111) apply note [18] to 'an absolute QEI evaluated on the corridor'. Neither site says that the corridor's sampled operator must be realised self-adjointly, with the absolute QEI holding on ALL of its domain. H3 as defined (noise.py:156-162) is a Minkowski statement about the smeared Wick-ordered operator on Hadamard vectors. Fewster-Smith gr-qc/0702056, the tree's RIGHT_INSTRUMENT (fewsterteo.py:181-183), bounds Hadamard states only. The corridor therefore needs a curved analogue of H3 (the Friedrichs extension from the corridor's Hadamard vectors, or those vectors forming a form core), and these two sites do not state one. ledger.py:584-597 (the D22 row) does append 'Or a failure of H3 ... a self-adjoint extension other than Friedrichs need not keep the bound', which carries the hypothesis there, but under a flat-space H3 label. Rederive E1-E5 shows the failure mode is real: -d^2/dx^2 on (0,oo) has form >= 0 on C_c^oo, yet its Robin extension psi'(0)=a psi(0), a<0, has eigenvalue -a^2 < 0.

ADDED/OVERSTATED: the word 'decides' claims a sharpness the note does not supply. Sites: noise.py:42-44 ('an absolute QEI evaluated on the corridor decides the distribution question there with no variance at all') and ledger.py:584-585 ('by FFR 1004.0179 note [18] it decides the distribution question there'). With a non-optimal bound Q, note [18] gives only supp mu_psi in [-Q,oo). That decides Prob(outcome <= -D) = 0 when D > Q, and decides NOTHING when D <= Q. Rederive D1-D3 shows this: with inf sigma = -1 and a valid bound Q = 2, the true probability is 1/3 at D = 0.5 and 0 at D = 1.5, and the bound is silent on both. N6 sharpness holds only in the Minkowski vacuum, and even there it is sharpness of inf sigma, not of a given QEI's value. The corridor's absolute QEI has NOT been evaluated (fewsterteo.py:149 O2_CLOSED = False; fewsterteo.py:184-187 records it as blocked on the mode functions), so which case obtains is unknown. ledger.py:1822-1826's own wording ('supported in the spectrum of the sampled operator, which an absolute QEI bounds below') is exact and does not overstate.

NOT drift, recorded for completeness: 'every measurement distribution mu_psi is supported in sigma(A_tau)' (noise.py:175-176) holds for every normalised psi in the Hilbert space and for every density matrix, not only for psi in D(A). If anything, the tree reads the result more narrowly than the spectral theorem allows.

later_literature.what: Sec. I p. 2: the smeared normal-ordered operators are 'defined, in the first instance, only as symmetric operators on a dense domain' and may have more than one self-adjoint extension. The Friedrichs extension is singled out, 'whose lower bound coincides with the sharpest possible quantum inequality bound. It is this operator that we have in mind.' Whether the operators are essentially self-adjoint 'is nontrivial and not fully resolved', and distinct extensions share vacuum moments. This paper is the source of the tree's H3, and it makes explicit the N1 hypothesis that note [18] states only as 'A is a self-adjoint operator'. Further: p. 3 restates the (b)=>(c) and Reeh-Schlieder parts. p. 12 sets the non-optimal Fewster-Eveson bound 27/128 against an estimated optimal 0.0236, which is the N7 gap between a QEI and inf sigma. p. 20: 'the conclusion that the probability distribution has a lower bound is independent of any concerns about uniqueness, because this follows from existing quantum inequality bounds'.

later_literature.what: p. 3 eq. (1.5): 'on general grounds [12], the infimum of the support is equal to the optimal quantum energy inequality', with the infimum taken over a dense core of states. p. 6: in 2D CFT the smeared stress tensor is self-adjoint on D(L_0) with a common core, so the N1 question is settled there. pp. 19 and 21: 'As is required on general grounds, the QEI bound therefore coincides with the infimum of the support', shown for two new infinite families of samplers. audits.lacked_data: Note [18] is a theorem of operator theory. Its conclusion depends on no measured quantity, so there is no datum the authors could have lacked that would move it, and M's hypothesis gets no grip on the equivalence itself. That is shown, not presumed: the published text has no numerical input (READ), and z3 proves the three implications with Q, the spectrum and the state weights all left free (A1-A4). What came later was mathematical, not empirical. FFR 1204.3570 (2012) made explicit that the self-adjoint realisation of the smeared operator is not unique in general ('not fully resolved'), and that the Friedrichs extension is the one whose lower bound is the sharp QEI. The tree already carries this as H3, marked LOAD-BEARING. Fewster-Hollands 1805.04281 (2018) settled self-adjointness for 2D CFT and confirmed again, on two new families, that the support infimum equals the optimal QEI. The one number the tree passes through the note (Q at b = 1 m) moves by 6.13e-10 relative between the tree's rounded HBAR and the exact SI-2019 value, which leaves 71.256 unchanged. So no missing datum changes the conclusion. The only gap is a hypothesis the tree's curved rows leave unstated (see drift), and that is not a datum.
audits.grade_evidence: The theorem itself STANDS exactly as published. It was READ in full at source (1004.0179v2 pp. 8-9). The three implications were machine-checked by z3 with vacuity guards (A1-A7) and illustrated at 30 digits on random Hermitian operators (B). The note's caveat was reproduced (C), and the paper's own closed forms were re-derived exactly (F1-F9). The later literature read here (1204.3570, 1805.04281) confirms it and corrects nothing. Its use in the FLAT theorem C1 (noise.py:165-177) is exact: self-adjointness comes via H3, the form bound is on the form domain, H6 = mu_psi, and only (a)=>(b)=>(c) is used. The grade is NARROWED rather than STANDS only because of the CURVED application at noise.py:42-44, ledger.py:584-585 and ledger.py:1822-1826 / LEDGER.md:111. (i) 'An absolute QEI ... decides the distribution question' holds only on the smaller class D > Q_corr, where Q_corr is the evaluated bound. A non-optimal bound gives support in [-Q_corr,oo) and nothing sharper (rederive D3: the bound is valid, the true probability is 1/3, and the bound is silent). Sharpness (N6) holds only in the Minkowski vacuum. (ii) Note [18] needs the bound on the whole domain of a self-adjoint realisation. On the corridor that is a curved analogue of H3, which these sites do not name: Fewster-Smith bounds Hadamard states, and rederive E shows a different extension can lose the bound. Neither point refutes anything, and neither is settled against the tree: Q_corr has not been computed (fewsterteo.py:149 O2_CLOSED = False), and ledger.py:1822-1826's own sentence ('supported in the spectrum ..., which an absolute QEI bounds below') is exact. Nothing here is WRONG, and no misprint was found in note [18].
audits.what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS, either of two things. (1) The curved rows state both conditions, e.g. 'decides, PROVIDED the evaluated absolute bound Q_corr satisfies D > Q_corr, for the Friedrichs extension of the corridor's sampled operator from its Hadamard vectors (a curved H3)'. (2) O2 is closed with Q_corr computed below D and the curved H3 named. To a sharper NARROWED (a demonstrated gap, still not WRONG of FFR): the corridor's absolute QEI is evaluated and gives Q_corr >= D, in which case note [18] decides nothing there. To WRONG: only a self-adjoint A with (a) holding on all of D(A) and sigma(A) not in [-Q,oo). z3 (A4) and the spectral theorem exclude this, and no such operator is known.

source.located: The theorem is a classic: Parseval 1799 for series, Plancherel 1910 for L^2(R). No arXiv copy exists, so the originals are NAMED-NOT-READ. The step the tree uses was READ at source in C.J. Fewster, 'Lectures on quantum energy inequalities', arXiv:1208.5399v1, at these places: p.3 and p.30 (Fourier convention fhat(k) = INT e^{ikx} f dx); p.10, eq (1) -> eq (3), where the m=0 Fourier bound -(1/16 pi^3) INT_0^oo |ghat|^2 u^4 du becomes -(1/16 pi^2) INT_R |g''|^2 dt, which is exactly the one-sided Parseval step with factor pi; pp.10-11, the W^{2,2}(R) regularity remark; p.29, eq (15), the two-sided form plus the remark '|ghat(u)|^2 is even'. The clamped boundary condition was READ in Fewster & Teo, arXiv:gr-qc/9908073v2, Prop. 2.1 (elements of W^{m,2}_0(I) vanish on the boundary together with their first m-1 derivatives), and in eqs (1.3)/(1.5), which give c_2 = 16 pi^2.

audits.published_statement: As restated at source in 1208.5399: p.10, eqs (1),(3), for m=0: (1/16 pi^3) INT_0^oo |ghat(u)|^2 u^4 du = (1/16 pi^2) INT_R |g''(t)|^2 dt, with fhat(k) = INT e^{ikx} f dx. p.29, eq (15): (1/32 pi^3) INT_R |ghat|^2 u^4 du = (1/16 pi^2) INT |g''|^2, which is INT_R |ghat|^2 = 2 pi INT_R |g|^2 applied to g''. The theorem behind it is standard and was not read in an original: the Fourier transform is a bijection of L^2(R) with INT |fhat|^2 = 2 pi INT |f|^2 in either e^{+-iut} convention.
published_hypotheses: f in L^2(R). The restatement's eq (1) is for g in C_0^oo(R); its own remark extends this to g in W^{2,2}(R), meaning g, g' and g'' exist distributionally and are square-integrable (1208.5399 p.10).
g is real-valued, so |ghat|^2 is even and INT_0^oo = (1/2) INT_R (1208.5399 p.25 and p.28).
FT(g'') = (-iu)^2 ghat with no boundary delta terms. This holds exactly when the zero extension lies in W^{2,2}(R), i.e. g = g' = 0 at both ends of the support (gr-qc/9908073 Prop 2.1).
The Fourier sign convention does not change |ghat|^2 for real g.
hypothesis_drift: noise.py:117-118 and 581-586 name only the series hypothesis. Three Plancherel hypotheses go unstated: (i) g is the one-sided cosine transform of S = k^3 n(k)/(2 pi^2); (ii) S is in L^2; (iii) ||g^2||_1 is a whole-line integral. All three hold, and this was COMPUTED (rederive A2, A4, A6b; noise.py:650 uses Y = 2 INT_0^oo, i.e. the whole line). Dropped from the statement but satisfied where it is used, so this is not a narrowing.
noise.py:583: the series identity holds only for x > 0. The integration range is x > 0, so this is satisfied (A1a).

noise.py:1043 checks only the series step (series = closed form), not the Parseval step INT_R g^2 = pi INT_0^oo S^2. That step is exercised only indirectly, by the spectral-convolution control at noise.py:1048 (tau = beta, 1e-8). This is a DISCREPANCY OF COVERAGE, not an error. Rederive A3 checks the step directly: rel 2.6e-30.

fewsterteo.py:46-54 and 301-303: the source's eq (1) is stated for smooth g, but the clamped-beam mode is not C^oo on R (g''(0) = g''(1) = 44.7466). The regularity is weakened, which the source's own W^{2,2} remark permits; the zero-extended mode is in W^{2,2} because g = g' = 0 at both ends (B1b, 3e-29). Not a narrowing.

fewsterteo.py:47-48: the 'clamped' hypothesis carries weight, and the tree states and checks it (fewsterteo.py:571-572). Guard B5i confirms it: without it, INT u^4|ghat|^2 diverges (per-period integral -> 4 pi^3 = 124.025) while pi INT (g'')^2 = pi^5/2 stays finite. No drift.

The normalisation INT g^2 = 1 is ADDED, but it is not a Parseval hypothesis, since the identity is homogeneous. It is needed only for the final equality with pi mu^4. Harmless.

fewsterteo.py:306-316: _tail keeps only the period average (g''(0)^2 + g''(1)^2)/U and drops the oscillating cross term -2 g''(0) g''(1) INT_U^oo cos(u)/u^2 du. audits.published_statement:
Abstract: 'After turning on an interaction that couples the two boundaries of an eternal BTZ black hole, we find a quantum matter stress tensor with negative average null energy, whose gravitational backreaction renders the Einstein-Rosen bridge traversable ... which we suggest might be related to quantum teleportation. However, it cannot be used to violate causality.'

Eq. (3.18): int_{U0}^inf dU T_UU = -h Gamma(2D+1)^2/(2^{4D}(2D+1)Gamma(D)^2 Gamma(D+1)^2 l) * 2F1(1/2+D,1/2-D;3/2+D;1/(1+U0^2))/(1+U0^2)^{D+1/2}. The paper says it is 'always negative' for 0<D<1 and zero at D=0.

Sec. 1: 'signals from early times on the horizon can intersect it again at late times, by passing through the directly coupled boundaries ... making them no longer achronal ... Hence the above impossibility results do not apply.'

Footnote 2: 'We do not consider the case of a time-independent interaction, in order to prevent the quantum state from becoming non-regular on the past horizon.'

Sec. 5, in prose with no calculation: 'The direct boundary interaction could then be produced by propagation through the ambient spacetime -- this would be the same as the interaction we studied, except with a time delay. A similar calculation would then lead to a traversable wormhole ... Since any infinite null geodesic which makes it through a wormhole must be chronal ..., such wormholes do not enable one to travel faster than light over long distances through space ... bank loan.'

Sec. 5, on teleportation: 'somewhat analogous ... Unlike the usual description of quantum teleportation, in our example it is essential that the channel ... is a quantum one ... we propose that the gravitational dual description of quantum teleportation ... is that the qubit passes through the ER=EPR wormhole'.
published_hypotheses: H1: the background is an eternal two-sided BTZ black hole (AdS3, l=1, beta=2 pi/r_h) with the bulk scalar in the Hartle-Hawking/TFD state. The paper 'expects' the D>3 case but does not compute it.
H2: the coupling is a relevant double-trace term h O_R(t) O_L(-t) with Delta<d/2, using the alternative quantisation and a bulk mass satisfying M^2 > -(d/2)^2 (eq. 1.2, footnote 4 on p.4).

H3: h(t) = h(2pi/beta)^{2-2D} for t>=t0 and zero before, uniform in phi (eq. 3.3). The case where the coupling is 'turned on at U0 and never shut off' is computed (Fig. 3.1a, eq. 3.18). The on-off case is the difference of two such results (Figs. 3.1b, 3.2). Footnote 2 excludes only a time-independent interaction.
H4: the calculation is first order in h, one loop, with large-N factorisation (eq. 2.9), and uses the linearised Einstein equation (1.3)-(1.5) with T_UU decaying faster than U^-2.
H5: the two-point function is chosen to be regular on the horizon. The authors say the global-mode construction 'is very tricky' and do not include it (footnote 4 on p.6).
H6: the Hadamard subtraction does not change when the boundary condition changes.
H7: the flat-space case, the Casimir reading, the no-faster-than-light 'bank loan' and the teleportation interpretation are discussion-section prose. They are not derived.
hypothesis_drift: phase1.py:137-140, 400-402, 482-483 and 544-546 (following amortize.py:43-50) write 'PER USE ... their own sentence closes it'. This adds an inference and attributes it to the source. The quoted words are verbatim from sec. 5. But that sentence says only how a flat-space coupling would be produced (by propagation through ambient space, with a delay). It says nothing about per use versus built once, and the next sentence is a prose expectation rather than a calculation. The source does support a narrower claim: each coupling pulse opens one short window (sec. 5: 'only open for a small proper time').

amortize.py:55-66, which phase1.py:146-148 relies on, says 'THEY DECLINED THE STANDING COUPLING'. That is broader than the source. GJW did compute a coupling that is switched on and then held (Fig. 3.1a, 'turned on at U = U0 = 1 and never shut off'; eq. 3.18 has no turn-off). Footnote 2 declines only an interaction that is time-independent for all t, including t -> -inf.

phase1.py:146-148 writes 'A TIME-INDEPENDENT CONFIGURATION'. The source says 'time-independent interaction'. The wording has drifted from the coupling to the configuration, and the geometry is time-dependent in every case GJW computed.

amortize.py:86-87 says 'the STANDING-COUPLING case is untested by anyone', and phase1 Theorem 5 inherits this. It is out of date against later work, though it is not a drift from 1608.05687 itself. Maldacena-Qi (1804.00491) built an eternal traversable wormhole from a time-independent coupling, and Maldacena-Milekhin-Popov (1807.04726) built one in flat space with a standing coupling carried by ambient exchange.

transit.py:11-13 and 276-277 say that GJW is quantum state teleportation. This drops the source's hedge ('suggest', 'propose', 'somewhat analogous') and drops GJW's stated difference: in their case the channel must be quantum. transit.py's own model (transit.py:37-39, 138-145: two classical bits, 'One pair, one transit') is the usual classical-channel picture that GJW set their mechanism apart from. This is an identification drift only, since transit.py computes nothing about GJW.

anecscope.py:109-113 has no drift. The external-causal-path non-achronality and the Casimir comparison both match the source (sec. 1). The owner leaves out the AdS double-trace context, which is an omission of context, not a changed claim.
