rederivation.outcome: ALL PASS (26 s). (1) sympy: -4 h Delta C0 times the (A.10) prefactor equals the (3.18) prefactor, ratio exactly 1, with C0 = sin(pi D)/(2^{2D+1} pi^2). (2) (A.14) is Gauss's second summation theorem; it checks to 1e-12. (3) The closed form (A.10) was compared with an independent quadrature of the triple integral in (A.9), the step before any hypergeometric identity is used: D=0.2,U0=1 gives 0.66920355 both ways; D=0.4 gives 0.51145883; D=0.6,U0=2 gives 0.19751668 (rel -5e-10); D=0.8 gives 0.8475805 (rel +2e-10). So the whole appendix chain is confirmed numerically. (4) (3.18) is below zero for every D in 0.01..0.99 and U0 in {0.1,1,2,10}. It tends to 0 as D->0. An earlier turn-on gives a larger |ANE|, and the on-off case stays negative. All of this matches the paper. (5) The tree's window table reproduces. Not checkable here in finite form: the one-loop two-point function (2.9), the unpublished horizon-regular mode choice (footnote 4), the linearised Einstein step, and every sec. 5 prose claim.

It is 'long': pi l > d always, with slope about 2.35 at large d. That is consistent with GJW's bank loan. later_literature.ref: arXiv:1908.03273 Fu, Grado-White & Marolf, Traversable asymptotically flat wormholes with short transit times (2019)
later_literature.what: Here t_min transit = d + logs, so t/d -> 1: it approaches the ambient light time but does not beat it. Footnote 8 notes that the 4D Shapiro delay has an IR log divergence, which makes it 'difficult ... to rigorously bound wormhole transit times'. GJW's bank-loan sentence is a heuristic whose rigorous 4D form is itself open. The traversability found is 'exponentially fragile'.
Further GJW-type constructions and a quantum-channel-capacity treatment. None contradicts (3.18).

audits.lacked_data:
In 2016 GJW had the BTZ two-point function, the TFD/KMS structure and linearised gravity; no measured constant enters. Three things came later: the time-independent coupling (Maldacena-Qi 2018), a flat-space standing-coupling realisation (MMP 2018) and flat-space transit times (FGWM 2019).

Does that later data change GJW's conclusion? No, on the evidence. (3.18) is re-derived here and confirmed numerically. The later cases extend the result rather than contradict it. The explicit flat-space constructions obey GJW's no-shortcut claim (MMP: pi l > d; FGWM: t/d -> 1 from above, up to logs), although FGWM note that a rigorous 4D bound is harder to state than GJW's sentence suggests.

What the later data do change is the tree's reading, not GJW. The per-use / not-reusable status the tree attributes to 'their own sentence' is not in that sentence. The standing-coupling case the tree calls 'untested by anyone' was tested in 2018 and gives a static, reusable (metastable) wormhole. That wormhole still has no speed advantage, so the tree's final refusal (no lead through a GJW-class channel) is corroborated, while the reason the tree gives for it is narrowed.
audits.grade_evidence:
The source result stands on its own terms. The (3.18) prefactor follows from the appendix (sympy ratio exactly 1). The chain (A.9)->(A.10) agrees with direct triple-integral quadrature to 1e-9 or better at four points. The sign is negative across 0<Delta<1 and zero at Delta=0. No datum enters.

The grade is NARROWED because the tree applies the paper to a larger or different class than the paper states:
(i) phase1.py:137-140, 400-402 and 544-546, following amortize.py:43-50, attribute 'PER USE ... CLOSED by the source' to 'except with a time delay'. That sentence says only how a flat-space coupling would be produced. Per-use holds for GJW's pulsed protocol as computed; it is the tree's inference, not the source's statement.
(ii) amortize.py:55-66, inherited by phase1.py:146-148, says GJW 'declined the standing coupling'. In fact GJW computed a coupling switched on and then held (Fig. 3.1a, eq. 3.18) and declined only the eternal interaction. Phase1 also writes 'configuration' where the source says 'interaction'.
(iii) The declined case has since been built (1804.00491, 1807.04726) and is static and reusable. So 'GJW ... reusable False' (phase1.py:400-402) is true of the 2016 protocol, not of the GJW class.
(iv) transit.py:11-13 drops GJW's hedge and their explicit statement that their channel must be quantum.

None of this is a computed contradiction. The tree's bottom line (no lead) is corroborated by MMP and FGWM. anecscope.py:109-113 matches the source.
audits.what_would_change_the_grade:
The grade would become STANDS if the tree restricted its GJW claims to the protocol as computed (pulsed coupling, AdS boundaries, first order in h); marked 'per use' as its own inference; quoted footnote 2 as 'time-independent interaction' and acknowledged the held-coupling case of Fig. 3.1a; updated the 'untested by anyone' claim against 1804.00491 and 1807.04726; and had transit.py carry GJW's 'propose' and quantum-channel qualifiers.

The grade would become WRONG for the tree's use if someone built a flat-space wormhole supported by a coupling that, once established, gives transits shorter than the ambient light time over long distances. None is known: FGWM reach t/d -> 1 from above, and for MMP pi l/d is always greater than 1, with slope about 2.35 at large d.

For the source result itself, the grade would change only if an error were found in (2.9) or in the unpublished horizon-regular mode choice of footnote 4. Neither can be checked here.

verifiers.lens: REFUTE THE GRADE (either direction) for 1608.05687, Gao-Jafferis-Wall, as the tree uses it
verifiers.reason:
I could not refute NARROWED in either direction. I checked every load-bearing reading against the source text and against the tree's own lines.

SOURCE, read in the saved v3 text, src/1608.05687.flat.txt
- The flat-space sentence in sec. 5 is quoted exactly: "The direct boundary interaction could then be produced by propagation through the ambient spacetime—this would be the same as the interaction we studied, except with a time delay." It says how a flat-space coupling would be produced. It says nothing about per use versus built once. The sentence after it, "A similar calculation would then lead to...", is an expectation in prose, not a calculation.
- Eq. 3.3 sets h(t,phi) = h(2pi/beta)^{2-2D} for t >= t0 and 0 for t < t0. That is a step function, held from t0 onwards.
- The caption of Fig. 3.1a reads "turned on at U = U0 = 1 and never shut off". Eq. 3.18 integrates from U0 to infinity with no turn-off.
- Footnote 2 reads "We do not consider the case of a time-independent interaction, in order to prevent the quantum state from becoming non-regular on the past horizon."
- So GJW did compute a coupling that is switched on and then held. The tree's line "THEY DECLINED THE STANDING COUPLING" (amortize.py:58) is broader than the source. That matters because amortize.py:62-64 describes the case it needs as one where you pay to "ESTABLISH the standing state", which is exactly the switched-on-and-held case of eq. 3.3. phase1.py:146-148 writes "configuration" where the source says "interaction".
- amortize.py:61-62 says "closed by the paper rather than by an argument of mine". phase1.py:137-140 says "Their own sentence closes it". Both attribute a per-use conclusion to the paper, and the paper does not state it. Per use does follow from GJW's pulsed protocol: sec. 5 says the wormhole "is only open for a small proper time" and that the astronaut must cross before it closes. The audit already grants this, so the drift is in the attribution and the scope, not in the per-use fact itself.
- The teleportation passage contains "somewhat analogous" and "Unlike the usual description of quantum teleportation ... it is essential that the channel ... is a quantum one". transit.py:11-13 and 276-277 drop that hedge. The audit has this right.

COMPUTATION
I wrote an independent mpmath evaluation of eq. 3.18 (verify/refute/gjw_318_check.py), separate from the auditor's script.
- It is strictly negative for all 99 values of D from 0.01 to 0.99, at U0 in {0.1, 0.5, 1, 2, 10, 100}.
- The on-off difference I(U0) - I(2U0) is also negative in every case.
- It tends to 0 as D -> 0 (-7.9e-13 at D = 1e-6).
- An earlier turn-on gives a larger |ANE|.
The source result stands on its own terms, so the grade cannot drop to WRONG on the source.

LATER LITERATURE, read at source through alphaXiv
- 1804.00491, p.2: "a traversable wormhole that is static and time independent, an eternal traversable wormhole". On p.52 the coupling arises "by integrating out the field modes" between two near-extremal black holes.
- 1807.04726, p.4: the interaction is "generated automatically by the exchange of massless fields in the bulk". p.19 gives pi l > d in all cases, with a slope "of order 2.35". p.23 gives a finite lifetime proportional to d^3/(q^2 l_p^2). So the wormhole is metastable.
- 1908.03273, abstract and pp.14-17: t_min = d + logs, and t/d -> 1. Footnote 8 names the 4D infrared log divergence in the Shapiro delay.
So amortize.py:84-87, "the STANDING-COUPLING case is untested by anyone", was overtaken in 2018. No later construction beats the ambient path, which corroborates the tree's bottom line and confirms that what is wrong is the reason the tree gives, not its conclusion. That is NARROWED, not WRONG.

WHY NOT STANDS
amortize.py states outright that the closure comes "by the paper rather than by an argument of mine", and amortize.py:68-69 calls the declined case "A NOT-RUN IN THE SOURCE". Fig. 3.1a and eq. 3.18 contradict the second claim as far as a held-after-turn-on coupling goes. These are statements about what the source says, and they are inaccurate, so STANDS is not supported.

MINOR AUDITOR OVERSTATEMENTS (none moves the grade)
(a) "FGWM reach t/d -> 1 from above". FGWM state d + logs, and say t_min >= d holds in D >= 5. In 4D the sign of the logs is not established; their footnote 8 is the reason. The "from above" should be dropped for 4D.
(b) Footnote 2 "declines only an interaction that is time-independent for all t, including t -> -inf". That is an inference from the stated reason (regularity on the past horizon) and from the contrast with the computed step function in eq. 3.3. It is sound, but it is not verbatim.
(c) Maldacena-Qi works in nearly-AdS2/SYK, not BTZ, and its state is the ground state of the coupled system, not the TFD. Calling it "the case footnote 2 declined" carries GJW's case across backgrounds. MQ does cite GJW [5] for the same kind of interaction.
(d) The canonical owner text for amortize.py's standing-coupling passage sits at lines 52-70. The audit cites 55-66, which is close enough and does not change the reading.

verifiers.reason:
REPRODUCED. I copied the script to verify/rederive/1608.05687.py and ran it. The output was ALL PASS in 19 s. The sympy prefactor ratio is exactly 1. The (A.10) closed form matches the (A.9) triple-integral quadrature with relative errors of -9e-13, 2e-16, -4.5e-10 and 1.5e-10. The sign grid, the D->0 limit, the monotonicity check and the on-off case all pass. The window numbers 2.6722e-7, 2.9026e-4 and 3.1330e-1 s all reproduce.

ENCODING. The script checks the published equations, not a toy version, and I compared each piece against the source text src/1608.05687.flat.txt. The C0 in check (1) is the C0 printed under (3.5), with beta = 2 pi/r_h and l = 1. The integrand in check (3) is the second line of (A.9) exactly as printed: (D+1) U1^(D+1) / [(U-U1 y)^D (U U1+y)^(D+2)], with y running from 1 to U/U1 and the U, U1 order swapped. Check (2) is (A.14) as printed.

GUARDS AND EXTRA CHECKS (scripts in verify/rederive/: vacuity.py, a9_line1.py, eq310_int.py).

Each mutation makes the check it targets fail, so no check passes vacuously:
- Changing Gamma(D+1)^3 to Gamma(D+1)^2 in (A.10) makes check (3) fail (rel 0.09 and 0.12).
- Changing the 2F1 argument from 1/(1+U0^2) to 1/(1+U0)^2 makes check (3) fail (rel 0.044 and -0.005).
- Changing 2^{4D} to 2^{4D+1} in the (3.18) prefactor gives ratio 2.0, so check (1) fails.
- Moving z from 1/2 to 0.45 in (A.14) gives ratio 0.893, so check (2) fails.
- Setting h<0 makes the sign check (4) fail.
- Setting D = 1.2 breaks H2 (D < d/2). The (A.9) integral then diverges (quad refuses alpha < -1), while the closed form gives a finite negative value (-0.797). So the check (3) agreement depends on 0 < D < 1.

Two checks go beyond the audit:
- I verified symbolically that line 1 of (A.9), after the derivative is taken, equals line 2. The difference simplifies to 0.
- I integrated the paper's main-text T_UU, eqs (3.10)-(3.14) with Appell F1, numerically over U and compared it with (3.18). At D = 0.3 the relative difference is -2.4e-5 with N = 24 and -1.1e-5 with N = 40. At D = 0.45 it is -1.1e-5 with N = 32. So the main-text formula and the appendix give the same integrated result. Pointwise they differ (for example, at D = 0.7, U = 8 the (3.10) value of T_UU is positive). That is expected, because (A.7)-(A.8) integrate by parts and drop a boundary term. It also matches the paper's remark that T_UU turns positive at late times.

MINOR CORRECTIONS. None of these moves the grade.
(a) The audit's outcome says 'the whole appendix chain is confirmed numerically'. It is not: (A.1)-(A.8) and the step from (2.9)/(3.6) to (A.9) line 1 are not checked by the audit's script. My (3.10) integration covers the main-text endpoint, but (2.9), the footnote-4 mode choice and the linearised Einstein step remain OPEN.
(b) The sign statement holds only for h>0. GJW write 'if we take positive h' (sec. 3) and 'with h > 0' (sec. 4). The script hard-codes h = 1, but no H1-H7 states h > 0. It should be a named hypothesis.
(c) Check (5) only re-checks the tree's arithmetic on GJW's D=3 heuristic, 'Delta t ≈ R ln(R/hL_planck)' (sec. 5). That formula assumes r_h ~ L_AdS ~ interaction time ~ R, and Delta t there is how far ahead of the turn-on the particle must be sent. Carried over to D=4 with G_N ~ L_P^2, the log doubles and so does every window (5.34e-7, 5.81e-4 and 6.27e-1 s). The audit says the L_planck value cannot move the result, and that is true. It misses the dimension extrapolation, which is a factor of 2 and leaves the '15 orders' conclusion in place.

GRADE. The source computation stands on the evidence. The NARROWED grade rests on how the tree reads the source, which is textual and outside this lens, and nothing in the re-derivation contradicts it. Not refuted.

verifiers.reason:
The numbers in the data rows are correct. The second row names its quantity wrongly, and the audit should be amended to say so. That does not change the grade.

Row 1 holds. Eq. (3.18) has no numerical physical input. It is a closed form in Delta, U0 and a dimensionless h. The 'no datum, so moves_conclusion No' entry is correct.

Row 2 values hold. scipy's NIST transcription has CODATA 2018 and CODATA 2022 both at 1.616255(18)e-35 m; it is in src/codata/_codata.py, txt2018 line 1439 and txt2022 line 1893. G is 6.67430(15)e-11 in both. Recomputing sqrt(hbar G/c^3) from the 2022 constants gives 1.6162550e-35. I read CODATA through that transcription, not through arXiv:2409.03787 itself. The windows recompute exactly: 2.6722e-7 s, 2.9026e-4 s and 3.1330e-1 s at h=1, matching amortize.py's table. Changing h from 1 to 1e-3 moves them by only 8.6%, 7.9% and 7.4%. So 'insensitive to L_planck' follows: it is a logarithm.

The defect the audit missed is in how row 2 labels its quantity. It calls it 'the traversal window dt ~ R ln(R/(h L_planck)) (GJW sec. 5)'. GJW never use the phrase 'traversal window'; a grep of the full source finds it nowhere. Sec. 5 says the wormhole is traversable 'if the particle is sent in before a time Delta t ≈ R ln(R/hL_planck) prior to the interaction being turned on'. It adds that sending more than 3/2 Delta t prior breaks the eikonal approximation. So Delta t is a lead time, of the order of the scrambling time. It is neither a window nor a transit duration. In GJW's words, the window is 'only open for a small proper time'. The formula also sits under GJW's stated assumption that r_h, L_AdS and the time the interaction is on are all of one scale R, in AdS. GJW give no such formula for flat space, so amortize.py:26-31, applying it to flat-space mouths of size R separated by D, is an extrapolation. audits.lacked_data:
In A09's own words, the authors lacked:
(a) any non-LTE study for P (p.15). One now exists (Andrievsky & Korotin 2026), and AG26 applies it as -0.07 dex, giving P 5.35.
(b) 3D non-LTE Li with complete UV background opacity. Wang+2021 supplies it, giving Li 0.96.
(c) Genesis solar-wind Ne and Ar.
(d) 3D non-LTE K.

Evidence FOR M's hypothesis: with the later data, the tree's 'P binds against a stellar photosphere' flips to Li on AAG21 (by 0.053 dex), on C11, and on L25 (by 0.6 %). On AG26 it survives by only 1.7 %; the margin shrinks from 0.037 to 0.007 dex.

Evidence AGAINST over-reading this:
(i) A09 is not shown wrong. Its quoted Li +-0.10 covers every later value and already gives Li a 36 % chance of binding, so the later data moved within A09's stated error.
(ii) The magnitude does not move on any compilation read here: 1.9e3 to 2.2e3 kg of stock per kg, or 134 to 154 t per 70 kg. Neither do 'a chondrite beats a star', 'site-selection criterion' or 'not a barrier'.
(iii) The CNO/metallicity dispute cannot affect the Li-P criterion, which does not depend on normalisation.

So the missing data matter for exactly one tree conclusion, which element binds, and A09's data never determined that in the first place.

audits.name: Implicit function theorem (local existence/sign of the branch root through gamma = 0)

source.located: Classical theorem: Cauchy (analytic case, first rigorous proof) and U. Dini (real variables, 1876; Lezioni di Analisi Infinitesimale vol. 1, Pisa 1907, pp. 197-241); no arXiv copy of either. Exact modern statement read in O. R. B. de Oliveira, 'The implicit and the inverse function theorems: easy proofs', arXiv:1212.2066v1 (2012), Theorem 1 (one equation, p. 5) and Theorem 2 (system, pp. 6-7). The function the tree applies it to was read at source in GMMPS arXiv:2604.01047v1: (4.17)-(4.18) p. 48, Thm 4.16 p. 58, (5.1)-(5.3) pp. 59-60, 5.3 p. 62.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries page text: 1212.2066 pp. 1-10 in full; 2604.01047 pp. 1, 33, 40, 48-52, 58-60, 62. Cauchy and Dini are NAMED-NOT-READ (restated in 1212.2066). Krantz-Parks (2002) is NAMED-NOT-READ; 1212.2066 p. 2 restates that the Krantz-Parks induction proof 'does not establish the local uniqueness of the implicit solution'.

audits.published_statement: de Oliveira 1212.2066 Theorem 1 (p. 5): 'Let F : Omega -> R be of class C^1 in an open set Omega inside R^n x R and (a, b) be a point in Omega such that F(a, b) = 0 and dF/dy(a, b) > 0. Then, there exist an open set X, inside R^n and containing a, and an open set Y, inside R and containing b, satisfying the following. For each x in X there is a unique y = f(x) in Y such that F(x, f(x)) = 0. We have f(a) = b. Moreover, f : X -> Y is of class C^1 and df/dx_j(x) = -F_{x_j}(x, f(x)) / F_y(x, f(x)).' Theorem 2 (pp. 6-7) is the same statement for F in C^1(Omega; R^m) with dF/dy(a, b) invertible. For m = 1 the sign condition > 0 in Theorem 1 loses nothing, since F can be replaced by -F.
published_hypotheses: H1 Omega open in R^n x R (here n = 1: x = alpha~^S_1, y = gamma)
H2 F of class C^1 on Omega
H3 F(a, b) = 0 at the base point
H4 dF/dy(a, b) != 0 (stated as > 0 in Theorem 1; invertible in Theorem 2)
THE CONCLUSION IS LOCAL: X and Y exist but have no stated size; uniqueness holds only inside Y; the theorem says nothing about zeros outside Y or about complex zeros
hypothesis_drift: H2 IS STRENGTHENED AND SATISFIED (linstab.py:959-960, 'F_S smooth near (0,0)'). Smooth implies C^1. This was checked, not assumed: F_S is affine in alpha (R4), and J is real-analytic on (-inf, 4m^2) (GMMPS (4.18) excludes only [4m^2, inf)). J(0), J'(0) and J''(0) are finite (R1). In effect there is no drift.

H4 IS KEPT, BUT THE APPLICATION USES CONDITIONS IT DOES NOT STATE (linstab.py:959-960). F_S'(0)(1-6xi)^2 kappa = 12 + kappa m^2/(24 pi^2) was re-derived. For this to be > 0 you need kappa > 0, m > 0 and xi != 1/6. z3 proves positivity under exactly those conditions, and a control shows kappa < 0 can flip the sign. m > 0 is stated at linstab.py:122. kappa > 0 and xi != 1/6 are left implicit (at xi = 1/6, F_S is undefined). All three hold in GMMPS's setting, so they are named here, not counted as dropped.

A WORDING DISCREPANCY IN THE CONCLUSION, NOT A REFUTATION (linstab.py:165-166, 345-346, 367-369; LEDGER.md:49). The tree says the branch zero 'exists iff alpha~^S_1 != 0'. The IFT actually gives a branch zero f(alpha) for every alpha in X, alpha = 0 included, with f(0) = 0. What follows from the IFT together with F_S(alpha,0) = -b_0 is that the branch zero is NONZERO iff alpha != 0 (R4, R5). The tree itself records gamma = 0 as an exact root at alpha = 0 (linstab.py:168-169, 961), so the meaning it intends is the accurate one; the literal word 'exists' is not accurate.

LOCALITY IS KEPT (linstab.py:164, 346-347, 367). To get from 'alpha near 0' to the physical alpha = 1/(64 pi^2), the tree uses an intermediate-value bracket at |b_2| <= 1e100 (linstab.py:636-661, 973-976), not the IFT. Measured here (R8): at GMMPS's point the IFT branch reaches the physical alpha iff b_2 >= -B*, with B* = F_1^2/(4 F_0) = 8.62e120 in m = 1 units. This holds for xi = 0 and for xi = 1/3; the two values coincide because B* scales as 1/(6(1/6 - xi)^2). Every b_2 > 0 is covered, and the tree's 1e100 bracket lies inside B*.

THE WORD 'grows' ADDS A DEPENDENCE, NAMED HERE (linstab.py:166, 963). The IFT gives only the SIGN of the root: f'(0) = -2 kappa m^4/(1 + kappa m^2/(288 pi^2)) < 0. Because F_S is affine in alpha, f is nonzero everywhere on X except at 0, so the sign is constant on each side of 0 throughout X, not just to first order. That a negative root is a growing mode is a separate result: GMMPS's pole term in (4.31) and Thm 4.16 (p. 58). The simple-zero condition that pole term needs is supplied by F_gamma != 0 along the branch.

THE SCOPE OF UNIQUENESS IS KEPT (linstab.py:173-180). The tree does not claim the 'only if' for growth in general. An extension computed here (R6): the winding number on |gamma| = 0.2 is 1, so there is exactly one zero in that complex disk and no complex-conjugate pair near the branch.

ADJACENT, NOT THIS KEY (belongs to the GMMPS Thm 4.16 entry). linstab.py:136 and 190 paraphrase Thm 4.16's growth clause as '(for Z strictly inside (-4m^2, 0))'. At source (p. 58) that interval belongs to the DECAY clause; the GROWTH clause reads 'Z subset (-4m^2, inf), with some gamma in Z, gamma > 0', in Q's variable. The tree's conclusion that the alpha = 0 root lies outside Thm 4.16 still holds under the source's own wording.

I tried to refute STANDS and could not. I read both sources myself through alphaXiv, and they match what the audit says.

1212.2066 Theorem 1 (p. 5) is quoted correctly: F is C^1 on an open set, F(a,b) = 0 and dF/dy(a,b) > 0. The conclusion is local, with X and Y of unstated size. The audit's restatement that the Krantz-Parks proof does not establish local uniqueness also appears on p. 2.

In GMMPS 2604.01047v1 I read the following at source:
- (4.17)-(4.18), p. 48: J is defined on D = C minus [4m^2, inf).
- p. 46: g, the Stieltjes transform of the measure ς(M)dM, is analytic off its cut [4m^2, inf). For J itself, analyticity at 0 follows from its integral form (4.17), and the audit's R1 checks it.
- (5.2), p. 59: a = 2m^2/(6xi-1), b0 = -alpha 4m^4/(6(1/6-xi)^2), b1 = -(2/kappa)/(6(1/6-xi)^2). b2 is free (p. 60).
- (5.3), p. 60: F_S = gamma(a-gamma)^2 J - (b0 + b1 gamma + b2 gamma^2).
- p. 60 also states kappa = 8 pi G.
- p. 58: Thm 4.16, and Q in (4.30).
- p. 62: 5.3, gamma ~ -b0/b1 = -16 pi G alpha m^4.
- p. 59: the (64 pi)^-1 misprint.

I re-derived the application independently with sympy (verify/refute/ift_check.py):
- J(0) = 1/(96 pi^2), computed by direct integration of rho from p. 52.
- F_S(0) = 24 alpha/(6xi-1)^2, which is zero iff alpha = 0.
- F_gamma(0) kappa (1-6xi)^2 = 12 + kappa/(24 pi^2), independent of b2.
- The slope is -2 kappa/(1 + kappa/(288 pi^2)), which is the tree's formula and does not depend on xi.
- F_S is affine in alpha (second alpha-derivative identically 0). So the branch zero vanishes only at alpha = 0 on all of X, which confirms R4.

B* = F1^2/(4 F0) reduces to 1.5 Omega_Lambda/(c Lambda), with c = 6(1/6-xi)^2:
- 8.622e120 from GMMPS's printed values.
- 8.605e120 with H0 = 67.4 and 7.328e120 with H0 = 73.04.
- Omega_Lambda cancels when Lambda is written as 3 Omega_Lambda H0^2, so B* scales as 1/H0^2 only.
- xi = 0 and xi = 1/3 give the same c (1/6), so they share B*.
- At its physical point the tree brackets only up to |b2| = 1e100, which lies inside B*.

I re-ran the audit's script: 27 PASS, 0 FAIL.

No hypothesis drift undermines STANDS:
- H2: C^1 holds; F_S is real-analytic at (0,0).
- H3: F(0,0) = 0 holds.
- H4: holds at GMMPS's parameters.

The two conditions the audit calls implicit are supplied at source. kappa = 8 pi G > 0 is READ on p. 60, and xi != 1/6 is forced by a = 2m^2/(6xi-1) in (5.2). So they are hypotheses of the setting, not dropped ones.

Small corrections to the audit. None of them moves the grade.
(a) The IFT's own non-degeneracy hypothesis needs only F_gamma(0) != 0. That holds for every kappa except 0 and -288 pi^2 (sympy solve). It is not true that kappa > 0 is 'needed' for the IFT to apply. kappa > 0, or kappa < -288 pi^2, is needed only for the '> 0' label and for the SIGN conclusion 'grows iff alpha > 0'. For -288 pi^2 < kappa < 0 the IFT still applies, but the slope flips. So in what_would_change_the_grade, 'kappa <= 0' should read 'kappa in (-288 pi^2, 0]', and kappa > 0 is READ at source anyway.
(b) The 'grows' step leans on GMMPS Thm 4.16 more than the audit says. Its growth clause, read at p. 58, requires Z subset of (-4m^2, inf), with the zeros of Q as the set Z. That is, every zero must be real, not only the branch zero. p. 60 says that for smaller b2 there are complex-conjugate zeros. So 'a negative root is a growing mode' carries a Thm 4.16 hypothesis beyond the simple-zero condition. That belongs to the Thm 4.16 entry, not to this key.
(c) The 'exists iff alpha != 0' wording. The IFT gives a branch zero for every alpha in X, alpha = 0 included, with f(0) = 0. The audit records this correctly as a discrepancy in wording, not a refutation. The tree itself records gamma = 0 as the exact root at alpha = 0, so the intended reading ('nonzero iff') is the accurate one.

Grading this key NARROWED or WRONG would turn a wording slip and an adjacent theorem's hypothesis into a fault of the IFT, which would over-represent the case against the tree. The later-literature gap, where the search was blocked by quota, is honestly marked NOT READ. The IFT is a theorem with no measured input, so that gap cannot move the grade.

audits.published_statement: Burgess gr-qc/0311082 p.4: predictions 'must be made within the context of a low-energy expansion, in powers of E/M ... What plays the role of the heavy scale M in the case of quantum gravity? It is tempting to identify this scale with the Planck mass, M_p^-2 = 8 pi G ..., and in some circumstances this is the right choice. But as we shall see M need not be M_p'. p.25-26: amplitudes suppressed by (E/M_p)^2, and by (E/4 pi M_p)^2 per loop; 'the weakness of the graviton's coupling follows only from the low-energy approximations, E << M_p and E << m'. p.35: validity needs the wavelength 'very small compared with the local radius of curvature'. p.46: leading quantum corrections 'controlled by the ratio l_p^2/r^2, where l_p = (G hbar/c^3)^1/2 ~ 1e-35 m ... At face value it is only for separations comparable to the Planck length that quantum gravity effects become important.' Garay gr-qc/9403008, abstract: 'The existence of a fundamental scale, a lower bound to any output of a position measurement, seems to be a model-independent feature of quantum gravity'. p.2: 'we set hbar = c = 1, so that the only dimensional constant is Planck's length l_* = sqrt(G); also, irrelevant numerical factors are ignored' ... 'the distance between two events will have a minimum uncertainty of the order of Planck's length. This conclusion, which has been reached by means of rather crude arguments'. p.3 (Mead, restated): Delta x >~ max(1/Delta p, l_*^2 Delta p) >~ l_*. p.4: 'these uncertainty relations are low-energy approximations to what the full theory of quantum gravity would give'. p.17: 'notions ... based on a metric structure lose their meaning at the Planck's scale'.
published_hypotheses: H1 (Burgess): GR plus matter is treated as a low-energy EFT. The control parameter is (E/M)^2, where M is the lightest heavy scale integrated out. M = M_p (reduced, M_p^-2 = 8 pi G) holds only 'in some circumstances'; M 'need not be M_p'.
H2 (Burgess p.35-38): short-wavelength modes are much shorter than the local curvature radius; backgrounds vary slowly ('nice slice'); time-dependent backgrounds need adiabatic vacua.
H3 (Burgess p.49-50): all-orders power counting is NOT demonstrated for general curved spaces. The breakdown scale is an estimate, 'not in serious doubt' but not proved.

H4 (Garay p.2-4): quantum mechanics, special relativity and GR are combined through thought experiments; numerical factors of order one are ignored; the bound is 'of the order of' l_*, from 'rather crude arguments' that are themselves low-energy approximations.
H5 (Garay abstract, p.17): 'seems to be a model-independent feature'. This is a claim about approaches to quantum gravity, not a measured fact; no datum at the Planck scale is used.

audits.lacked_data: M's hypothesis, tested for this result. What the authors had: hbar, c and G, dimensional analysis, and thought experiments (Mead 1964 as Garay restates it; Burgess's power counting). What they lacked, and what no one has yet: any measurement at or near l_P. The location of the breakdown is an extrapolation by construction (Garay p.2, 'rather crude arguments'; Burgess p.49-50, curved-space power counting 'not yet given'). The only numerical input that could have moved, G, has not moved (CODATA 2018 = 2022), and it cannot move the crossovers in Planck units at all, because R/l_P depends only on Lambda. Evidence on the missing datum, in each direction: (a) toward a LOWER breakdown energy (larger length): Burgess p.4, 'M need not be M_p'. If so, the tree's sub-Planckian crossovers sit even further outside the framework and the refusal gets stronger. (b) toward NO breakdown (a UV completion within QFT): not read here because the later-literature search was unavailable, so this direction is OPEN. So the authors did lack data, and the gap is real and will not close soon. None of the data that can be obtained moves the tree's conclusion. The datum that cannot be obtained could move only the words 'outside the domain of the theory' and 'exactly', not the rough location of the crossovers.
audits.grade_evidence: As published (Burgess gr-qc/0311082 p.4, 25-27, 46; Garay gr-qc/9403008 p.2-4, 17), the extrapolation says semiclassical GR+QFT is expected to lose control at separations 'comparable to' or 'of the order of' l_P. Numerical factors are ignored, the scale M 'need not be M_p', and the curved-space power counting is not demonstrated. The tree's crossover_is_sub_planckian holds in every Planck convention tried, and at the crossovers the required curvature is itself at the Planck scale (l_P^2 G rho/c^4 = 1.056 and 0.732). So the tree's central claim STANDS to within an order-one factor: the Ford-Roman and Casimir crossovers lie where the framework cannot be trusted. The grade is NARROWED for four reasons. (i) The tree uses a sharp boundary and a band test [0.1, 10] that depend on a convention it never names. Under the reduced Planck length Burgess uses, two of the three crossovers fall outside the band (0.0614 and 0.0738), and the z3 window [26.46, 2513] excludes Lambda = 9.98. (ii) It says 'exactly where', while the sources say 'of the order of' and 'need not be M_p'. (iii) It states the boundary with no status word, though the sources call it an estimate. (iv) It rules out an EFT cutoff at a few l_P, where Fliss et al. treat a Planckian cutoff as inside the EFT; their own condition |8 pi G xi phi^2| = 2.518 xi at the tree's cutoff rules it out only for xi >~ 0.40. No datum has moved (G and l_P are unchanged in CODATA 2022). This is not WRONG: nothing here refutes the tree's structural finding, and the spread of 10.26 is exact whatever Lambda is.
audits.what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the owner names two hypotheses (the non-reduced l_P convention and the order-one status of the boundary), replaces 'exactly' with 'to within an order of magnitude', and conditions the NMC exclusion on xi (or cites a passage where Fliss et al. put the breakdown at a few l_P regardless of xi). To OPEN on the domain claim: later literature (species bound, asymptotic safety), once read, showing that a UV completion keeps semiclassical control below l_P. That would turn 'outside the domain of the theory' into 'outside the domain of the perturbative EFT'. To WRONG: only a computed case in which a crossover lies well above the breakdown scale in every convention. None was found: FR needs Lambda >= 105.3 and Casimir needs Lambda >= 72.95 to reach even the non-reduced l_P.

I am refuting the grade. OPEN rested on one premise, that the source could not be read, and that premise no longer holds. In this session alphaXiv returned arXiv:0911.1955v2 in full, through both answer_pdf_queries and get_paper_content with fullText.

READ AT SOURCE, Fixsen 2009:
- Abstract, p.1: FIRAS recalibrated with WMAP gives 2.7260±0.0013. The value from the literature is 2.72548±0.00057 K.
- Table 2, p.5: 16 measurements, Mean 2.72548, uncertainty .57 mK.
- p.5: without the FIRAS measurements, "the weighted average is 2.729±0.0038 which is 1.0 σ from the final answer". The audit marked its 2.729±0.004 as a second-hand attribution. It is now READ, and 0.004 is the rounded 0.0038.
- p.5: "97%" of the weight is FIRAS. χ²=17.9 for 15 DOF, expected "about 26% of the time".

I recomputed Table 2 as an inverse-variance weighted mean (verify/data/wmean_0911.1955.py):
- mean 2.72549 ± 0.00057
- non-FIRAS 2.7294 ± 0.0038, 1.01σ from the mean
- CN 2.7420 ± 0.0173, against the printed 2.742±0.017
- FIRAS weight 97.8%
- p(χ²≥17.9 | 15 DOF) = 0.268
One discrepancy, recorded only: the recomputed χ² is 18.07 against the printed 17.9. That is a discrepancy, not a refutation.

value_then: right in substance. One unread hypothesis was described wrongly. The audit called WMAP's calibration "dipole-based". At source (p.1) the calibration comes from the spacecraft's velocity relative to the Sun, known to under 1 cm/s; the dipole is only added back into the velocity maps afterwards. The hypotheses READ at source:
- the blackbody form plus the first-order Doppler expansion (Eqs. 1-2)
- a 15% sky cut
- WMAP channel/year errors are uncorrelated (p.4)
- a 50 mK cutoff for choosing which literature values to include (p.5)
- the 16 inputs, three of them FIRAS calibrations of one instrument, are combined as independent in a weighted mean.
These should be NAMED hypotheses.

value_now: the audit says NOT READ. It can now be partly filled. Planck 2018 VI (1807.06209v4, p.14, footnote 14) READ: "We take T0 = 2.7255K (Fixsen 2009), with the ±0.0006K error having negligible impact." Ivanov, Ali-Haïmoud and Lesgourgues (2005.10656v2, Eq. 1) READ: they use 2.72548±0.00057 K as the current value and call it "confirmed by several independent experiments". PIXIE is named only as a future improvement. Neither read source names a superseding absolute measurement through 2020-21. PDG 2024 remains unread.

Row 2, z_rec, is NARROWED. Planck 2018 VI Table 2 (p.16) READ: z* = 1089.92 ± 0.25 for TT,TE,EE+lowE+lensing, a base-ΛCDM derived parameter. The audit's drift entry says this is model-fit and marks that NOT READ; it is now READ and confirmed. But footnote 14 shows that z* was computed with T0 held at Fixsen's 2.7255. So the audit's sentence "the number rests on Planck's z_*, not on Fixsen" overstates the independence. Ivanov et al. (p.2) say that at fixed baryon-to-photon and dark-matter-to-photon ratios the temperature of recombination is fixed, so physically 1+z* = T_rec/T0 does depend on T0 (the audit's R1b). The code's ratio is still tautological, because z is hard-coded, so drift (i) against the tree stands. The physical dependence on Fixsen exists, but it is indirect.

moves_conclusion: "No" still follows, but R7's range is too narrow. Ivanov et al. Table I (p.15) READ gives:
- Planck-only T0 = 3.144 (+0.17/−0.065) K, outside R7's [2.4, 3.0]

At T_rec held at 2973.3 K, 1+z runs from 945.7 to 1159.6 (verify/data/later_T0_0911.1955.out), so the verdict, ratio ≠ 1, holds. The audit also says the Landauer count moves by "0.13% at most across the values named". Over these READ values it moves −13.3% to +6.3%. massform says no verdict rests on that note, so the moves_conclusion answer does not change, but the 0.13% bound is too small.

lacked_data: the audit says M's hypothesis "stays untested". It can now be answered with READ evidence, and that evidence goes against M's hypothesis for this result:

- The only contrary value, Planck+SH0ES, depends on assuming ΛCDM, and its own authors say BAO "arbiter[s] in favor of Planck + FIRAS".

Proposed grade STANDS, for 2.7255 K as the tree uses it: 0.035σ from 2.72548, and the same rounding Planck itself prints. Drift (i) and the massform fifth-digit finding stay recorded against the tree, not the source.

audits.lacked_data: What the authors had, according to the summaries: a single Yb+ ion, composite-pulse Ramsey with coherence above 1 s, a sidereal fit in the Sun-centred frame, and a theoretical matrix element. What came later: no newer electron c_JK measurement was found. A recalculation of the matrix element could shift the bound by an O(1)-O(10) factor; that was not checked. Does data the authors lacked change the tree's conclusion? No, and this was computed: '42 orders short at r = 38.6 um, beta = 1' survives a revision of the bound by up to ~40 orders either way (rederive (b)). The gaps that matter are in the tree's own data. (1) B, the lab velocity relative to the compactification frame, is unmeasured and is needed to project KN's c onto the components Dreissen bounds; under a hypothetical structure its absence makes the tree's comparison conservative. (2) r is fixed at its largest allowed value, where the bound bites least. No datum the authors lacked has been shown to move anything here.
audits.grade_evidence: The source could not be read in this stage. alphaXiv refused every call on quota, and every publisher and repository host was blocked by the egress proxy. So the 1e-21 marked 'READ' at branelink.py:149 has not been checked against the paper's table, and its hypotheses (electron sector; Sun-frame spatial c_JK; other coefficients zero; confidence level) are known only from search summaries. By the docket's rule an unreadable claim is OPEN, not STANDS. What was computed: the tree's arithmetic is exact (|c| = 6.372e-64, 42.196 orders, rounded to 42), and O7's SME null does not change for any bound value within about 40 orders, so no plausible correction to the datum moves it. Two scope notes are recorded, not repaired. (i) The tree probably drops a hypothesis: the bound applies to c_JK components, not to a scalar |c|, and the projection needs the unmeasured B. Under a hypothetical structure this drop is conservative. (ii) LEDGER.md:101 and ledger.py:1793 restate the null without the (r = 38.6 um, beta = 1) qualifier, and at beta = 1 the same bound does bite for r <= 3.08e-26 m. Nothing here is WRONG, and no error in Dreissen et al. is shown.
audits.what_would_change_the_grade: Read arXiv:2206.00570 (the fitted c_JK table with uncertainties and confidence level, the matrix element, the frame and the sector) and Kabat & Nomura eqs. 76-77 (the tensor structure, the definition of mu, and the sentence quoting ~1e-21). If the components are bounded at no more than a few x 1e-21 in the electron sector, Sun-centred frame, the value STANDS. The tree's comparison would then be NARROWED on the component/frame hypothesis, unless KN's c maps onto c_JK with O(1) weight independent of B. If KN's c is c_TT-type in the compactification frame, the comparison is NARROWED in the conservative direction. If the table shows the relevant components are bounded only at 1e-19 or weaker, the value is a discrepancy, but rederive (b) shows the conclusion moves by no more than 2 orders.

verifiers.lens: REFUTE THE GRADE (OPEN) for dreissen-sme-lab-bound
verifiers.reason:
The audit graded OPEN only because neither source could be read. Both are readable now, and I read them at source through alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries: arXiv:2206.00570v4 pp. 1-3, 5-7, 9-10 and arXiv:2309.05759v2 pp. 1-26 including refs. Once read, the evidence supports a definite grade, so OPEN does not hold.

(1) THE VALUE STANDS AS PUBLISHED. Dreissen et al., abstract and §2.5: "constrain all the coefficients of the c_MN tensor now at the 10^-21 level", tightest 3.9e-21 on c_XY. Table 1, all 1σ: c_X-Y = (-5.2±7.8)e-21, c_XY = (4.4±3.9)e-21, c_XZ = (-5.0±9.3)e-21, c_YZ = (6.3±8.9)e-21, all within about 1.1σ of zero. KN p. 25 quotes it with ref. [14] = Dreissen: "laboratory bounds on the dimensionless coefficients c_mu nu have reached the level of ~10^-21". So the tree's 1e-21 is the paper's own order-of-magnitude headline. Per component the 1σ uncertainties are 3.9-9.3e-21, so the figure overstates by at most about 1 order. That is a discrepancy, not an error. The audit's rederive (b) already shows the conclusion does not move.

(2) THE USE IS NARROWED, on dropped hypotheses that are now READ rather than inferred.
(a) Sector. The bound is on the combined electron-photon tensor c'_mu nu = c_mu nu + k_mu nu/2, traceless and symmetric (p. 2). It is not on the electron's c alone. KN's "for the electron" sentence already drops this, and the tree inherits the drop.
(b) Components. Only the anisotropic spatial SCCEF components c_X-Y, c_XY, c_XZ and c_YZ are bounded (eqs. 5 and 11). The c_TJ terms enter only through the β boosts and are removed by the 5 µHz high-pass filter. c_TT and the isotropic parts are not bounded at all.
(c) What the tree compares. branelink.py:288-292 codes 0.75·β² = b_0b_0 - ¼η_00 b², which is the c_00 component in the frame where b is purely timelike. KN eq. 76 gives the structure b_mu b_nu - ¼η_mu nu b², which in that frame is c_TT plus an isotropic spatial trace. Neither is a quantity Dreissen bounds. Anisotropic SCCEF components arise only through the lab's velocity relative to the b-frame, which is O7's unmeasured B. So the scalar |c|-vs-1e-21 comparison is not like-for-like. It is conservative, as the audit's (e1) supposed, and that structure is now READ in KN rather than hypothesised.
(d) Dropped hypotheses of KN eq. 77, settling the audit's "UNVERIFIED mu" item. μ is the bulk-graviton IR regulator or mass, so μr→0 is exact for a massless graviton. But eq. 77 also assumes m = 0, a massless brane fermion, and b² ≈ 0. My numerical check (verify/refute/dreissen_refute.py) reproduces -ζ(3)/4 = -0.300514 at m = 0, b² = 0. Each assumption fails where the tree evaluates:
- Electron mass. For the electron at 38.6 µm, πm_e r/ħc = 3.1e8. The integral falls roughly as 1/(πmr)²: it is 0.0014 of its massless value already at πmr = 100. That pushes the coded figure roughly 16 more orders short.
- β = 1. The tree evaluates at β = 1, i.e. b² = 1, using the b² ≈ 0 asymptote. The full massless I_grav grows steeply with b²: ×3.5 at 0.5, ×54 at 0.9, ×1953 at 0.99. This pulls the other way, and its size at exactly b² = 1 was not established.
So "42 orders short" is the number of a coded asymptote outside its stated domain, not KN's eq. 76 for an electron. At the tree's own β_max = 3.74e-8, b² ≈ 0 holds and only the m = 0 drop remains. That drop is conservative: it makes the null more short, not less.

(3) WHAT IS NOT SHOWN. No error in Dreissen et al. No error in KN. Nothing flips "does not bite at r = 38.6 µm". The conclusion is NARROWED to the conservative direction, with a scope note recorded and nothing repaired. The audit's arithmetic, 6.372e-64 and 42.196 orders, is correct as coded. The "(READ)" provenance mark at branelink.py:149 is consistent with either route, because KN cites the same 1e-21 to Dreissen.

audits.name: Kibble-Zurek mechanism: rapid quench through symmetry breaking gives a topological-defect network

source.located: T.W.B. Kibble, 'Topology of cosmic domains and strings', J. Phys. A 9 (1976) 1387; W.H. Zurek, 'Cosmological experiments in superfluid helium?', Nature 317 (1985) 505. Both pre-arXiv. Intended restatements: A. del Campo & W.H. Zurek, arXiv:1310.1600 (IJMPA 2014), identity corroborated only by a WebSearch listing; W.H. Zurek, Phys. Rep. 276 (1996) 177, cond-mat/9607135.

audits.published_statement: NOT READ at source, so no verbatim quotation is offered. For orientation only, and graded on nothing, the standard statement is usually taken to be as follows. Kibble 1976: at a symmetry-breaking transition G -> H the order parameter lives on the vacuum manifold M = G/H. Causally disconnected regions choose points of M independently, and topologically stable defects form, their type fixed by the homotopy of M (pi_0 walls, pi_1 strings, pi_2 monopoles). Zurek 1985: for a quench through a continuous transition, critical slowing down tau ~ tau0/|eps|^(z nu) makes the dynamics freeze out at t^ ~ (tau0 tau_Q^(z nu))^(1/(1+z nu)). That sets the domain size xi^ = xi0 (tau_Q/tau0)^(nu/(1+z nu)) and a defect density ~ xi^-(D-d). A WebSearch paraphrase of 1310.1600 is consistent with this but is not a read.
published_hypotheses: (as usually stated; NOT READ) a symmetry-breaking phase transition G -> H with a genuine order parameter
(Zurek; NOT READ) the transition is continuous (second order): relaxation time and correlation length diverge at the critical point (critical slowing down), with exponents nu and z

(Kibble; NOT READ) the vacuum manifold G/H has a nontrivial homotopy group pi_k for the defect (pi_0 walls, pi_1 strings, pi_2 monopoles in 3 space dimensions); only then are the defects topologically stable
(both) causally disconnected or dynamically uncorrelated regions choose independently; the quench rate relative to the relaxation time sets the domain size
(gauge theories; NAMED-NOT-READ: Hindmarsh-Rajantie flux trapping, geodesic rule) for a gauged order parameter the 'phase' is gauge-dependent, and defects are set by gauge-invariant windings or flux

So in 3 space dimensions there are no topologically stable walls, strings or monopoles.

rederivation.outcome: 16/16 checks PASS, exit 0. A (sympy): H^dag H = |x|^2, so the vacuum manifold is S^3. An explicit SU(2) matrix with U^dag U = 1 and det U = 1 carries (0, v/sqrt2) to every vacuum (transitive), and 4 - 1 = 3 = dim S^3. B (numeric witnesses, seed 67): pi_0 by a great-circle arc; pi_1 by 20 random Fourier loops; pi_2 by 10 random smooth 2-spheres. Exponents: 1/4 (mean field) and 0.2866 (3D XY, with nu from memory). In a crossover model with d = 0.05, xi^ saturates at xi_max = 4.4721 for tau_Q >= 1e6, while the critical xi^ keeps growing as tau_Q^(1/4). audits.lacked_data: Kibble (1976) and Zurek (1985) lacked the Higgs mass (discovered 2012) and the lattice result that the SM electroweak transition is a crossover above ~72 GeV (1996 on; 1508.07161 at m_H = 125 GeV). Having that data does not change the KZ mechanism itself. Nothing read or computed here refutes it within its hypotheses, and the re-derived freeze-out algebra agrees with the standard form. What the later data changes is whether the mechanism applies to the SM. (i) There is no true transition, so critical scaling does not apply (C3). (ii) The vacuum manifold S^3 has trivial pi_0 to pi_2 (A, B). That fact involves no datum and was available in 1976, so it is not a data gap of the authors; it is a hypothesis the tree drops. Evidence the other way: the tree's conclusion QUENCH_GIVES_A_TEMPLATED_OBJECT = False is not moved. For a rapid quench the crossover and critical models give the same domain size (C5, 0.03%), and nothing read here gives a template a way to bias the ordering. That is an absence of a mechanism, not a theorem. Whether uncorrelated EW domains relax to a uniform vacuum is not established here. M's hypothesis is not supported for this result: the later data narrows where the tree may invoke Kibble and Zurek, not what they said.
audits.grade_evidence: The source could not be READ (alphaXiv quota exhausted on all three tools; arXiv, ar5iv, Wikipedia, Nature and APS egress-blocked), so the published wording and exponents stay OPEN and no quotation is offered. (1) A computation here: the SM Higgs vacuum manifold is S^3 (sympy A1-A5) with trivial pi_0, pi_1, pi_2 (numeric witnesses B1-B3). A topological defect is by definition a nontrivial homotopy class, so the 'TOPOLOGICAL DEFECT NETWORK' of warpfolder.py:77-79 has no stable walls, strings or monopoles in the SM case the owner applies it to, whatever the sources' wording. (2) The tree's own READ: massform.py:1127-1136 quotes 1508.07161 fn.1, 'no real symmetry breaking phase transition', and warpfolder.py:69 itself says 'the crossover', against warpfolder.py:77 'a symmetry-breaking transition'. In a crossover model the freeze-out length saturates (C3). So the result holds on a smaller class (continuous transitions with nontrivial homotopy) than the tree uses (the SM EW crossover). It is NOT WRONG: nothing refutes the KZM within its hypotheses, and the tree's conclusion 'not a templated object' is not contradicted (C5). It is NOT DATA-DEPENDENT for the external result: the homotopy fact involves no datum. Downstream, S9 (LEDGER.md:66) and R11 (specthm.py:1181-1182) do not read QUENCH_GIVES_A_TEMPLATED_OBJECT, and the owner states that (a), (b) and (c) are each independently sufficient (warpfolder.py:107); (a) and (c) are not audited here. audits.what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the owner restricts (b) to 'uncorrelated domains, no templating channel' with the vacuum manifold and the crossover named as hypotheses, and a verbatim read of Kibble 1976 and Zurek 1985 (or 1310.1600 or cond-mat/9607135) confirms the statement and hypotheses as restated. To OPEN: if the homotopy computation is set aside because it is not a read, nothing checkable remains and the grade falls to OPEN for want of the source. NON-CONVERGENCE CLAIM (hpscentre.py:171-172: 'a has not converged to a constant in either system: it keeps rising with the window'). The extrapolated limit depends on the tail model assumed: printed 5.64 under a power-law tail, 6.75 under a 1/ln l tail. These data do not determine a limit. The tree's wording claims only non-convergence within the range, so this is not a drift.

ASYMPTOTIC-FLATNESS PHRASING. The WebSearch abstract snippet says 'two asymptotically spatially flat regions'. Hochberg-Visser gr-qc/9802046 p.3, with an HPS author, says 'no asymptotically flat spatial regions'. The tree quotes HPS as 'the metric as a whole is not asymptotically flat' (hpscentre.py:99-100). The far-zone law makes g_tt unbounded, so the full metric is not asymptotically flat on any of these readings. The wording difference between the snippet and the later paper is recorded as a discrepancy and not adjudicated.

audits.published_statement: Not quoted from source in this stage. As transcribed by the tree's DOCKET 62 read and not re-read here: F&T Sec. 7 evaluates their static-spacetime bound (2.12) for a massless, minimally coupled scalar in the Boulware (static) vacuum, on the Schwarzschild exterior r > 2M, for a static observer. It uses Candelas' asymptotic mode sums (7.4)/(7.5), which split the modes into outgoing ('up', from the past horizon) and ingoing ('in', from past null infinity) families, with greybody (horizon transmission) coefficients B_l(w) in (7.6). Proper time enters through (7.7), tau_0 = |g_tt|^{1/2} t_0. The bound (7.8) has a (1-2M/r)^{-1} pole and goes arbitrarily negative at the horizon. (7.10) is the comparison form, stated to lie 'between 9/64 and 1/4' of Pfenning & Ford's Schwarzschild bound, because its (tau_0/r)^2 coefficients are 16/9 of Pfenning-Ford's. The arithmetic (9/64)(16/9) = 1/4 is checked here.
published_hypotheses: Globally static spacetime of class (2.1): ds^2 = -|g_tt| dt^2 + g_ij dx^i dx^j. Read by DOCKET 62, not re-read here.

Free real scalar, minimally coupled, massless in Sec. 7. Normal ordering is relative to the static (Boulware) vacuum, so the bound is on <:rho:> and not on rho_ren. Read by DOCKET 62; a1/o5.txt:3 quotes Sec. 2.

audits.published_statement:
Sec. IX: 'Their true value is not so much that they actually rule out topology change, but rather that they allow us to pinpoint what modifications we have to make in our general framework so as to allow it. A popular modification ... is to abandon the Lorentzian framework altogether and to use a Euclidean path integral formalism. But even within the general Lorentzian framework there are still several interesting possibilities.'

A] Dropping causal compactness: Tipler Thm 5 '(in the closed universe case) ... if topology change occurs via a non-compact interpolating spacetime, then it contains (under some mild additional assumptions) a singularity (in the sense of an incomplete timelike geodesic) or a point at infinity'. A singularity specifically follows 'only under the significant additional assumption' of an upper bound on timelike lengths. 'The presence of points at infinity is still a highly undesirable feature.'

B] Weakening the curvature constraints: 'This would not affect the presence of causality violations, but it might permit topology change as a dynamical process.' Either alter Einstein's equation ('such an alteration would have to be fairly severe'), or allow 'violations of the energy conditions large enough to allow assumption (ii) to be violated. Some discussions of wormhole creation are, for example, based precisely on large violations of the energy condition.'

C] Degenerate metrics: 'allow the metric to vanish or to become degenerate at isolated points and to use these kinds of singularities in order to get topology change ... even in standard general relativity (couched in first-order language) Horowitz has shown that it is possible to construct reasonable topology-changing spacetimes if degenerate metrics are allowed. So, this might well prove to be the correct approach to describing topology change.' Borde adds that the usual causal structure 'will not necessarily be well-defined'.

Sec. VIII: 'If we were satisfied with metrics that are only continuous ... S1 and S2 need not be diffeomorphic, even if causality violations are forbidden.'
published_hypotheses: Borde's list is framed as non-exhaustive: 'several interesting possibilities' inside the Lorentzian framework, plus the Euclidean route outside it. The routes are offered as modifications that 'allow' topology change, not as a proof that every way out fails.

Every escape is measured against the paper's framework: a smooth, non-degenerate, time-oriented Lorentz metric on a causally compact interpolating manifold. 'All of these comments are valid only under the assumptions of this paper.'

audits.published_statement: Low gr-qc/9812067, restating Wald Ch.10 and Hawking-Ellis Ch.7. Thm 2.4 takes an initial data set (Sigma,h,K,J,rho) whose matter u obeys a quasilinear symmetric hyperbolic system A^a nabla_a u + B u = c (eq. 2.2), with T depending only on u and g. It then states: (1) there is a unique smooth maximal development, globally hyperbolic with Cauchy surface i(Sigma); (2) if two data sets agree on S, then D(i(S)) is isometric in the two developments; (3) g depends continuously on the data. Cor 3.1/4.1: if the data change only inside K = J^+(p) cap Sigma, D(i(Sigma\K)) stays isometric, and 'no gravitational influence propagates faster than light'. audits.lacked_data: The result is a theorem, and no measured number enters it; only the matter model's principal part (H2) does. The authors lacked a measurement of the speed of gravity. GW170817 supplied it in 2017, -3e-15 <= (v_gw-c)/c <= 7e-16, which confirms speed c and moves the tree's floor by less than 1e-14 (C8). That is evidence AGAINST M's hypothesis for this result. They also lacked any established model of the exotic matter the corridor needs, and that is still missing. Classical exotic fields with a causal principal part leave the theorem unchanged (C7). For quantum sources, well-posedness is not established (2604.01047). A superluminal matter sector would lower the floor (C6). So the missing data do not overturn the theorem, but whether H2 holds for whatever would actually build the corridor is still OPEN. The later correction on the DEC (Earman, Geroch, Wong) applies to Low's Thm 4.2 step, which the tree does not use.

audits.published_statement: Carroll gr-qc/9712019 ch.6: in harmonic gauge, Box hbar_mu_nu = -16 pi G T_mu_nu (6.22). 'it is straightforward to derive the weak-field metric for a stationary spherical source such as a planet or star ... h_00 = -2Phi (6.24), where Phi is the conventional Newtonian potential, Phi = -GM/r. Let us now assume that the energy-momentum tensor of our source is dominated by its rest energy density rho = T_00 ... Then the other components of T_mu_nu will be much smaller than T_00, and from (6.22) the same must hold for hbar_mu_nu.' This leads to (6.25) h = hbar_00, and so (re-derived here, R1) to ds^2 = -(1+2Phi)dt^2 + (1-2Phi)dx^2. That equals exact isotropic Schwarzschild to O(M): -g_tt = 1 - 2M/r + 2M^2/r^2 + ..., g_ii = 1 + 2M/r + (3/2)M^2/r^2 + ...

audits.published_statement: v1 p.5, quoted verbatim from the text layer: 'We propose that the extent to which the semiclassical approximation is violated can be measured by the dimensionless quantity Delta_{abmn}(x,y) = |(<:T_ab(x)T_mn(y):> - <:T_ab(x):><:T_mn(y):>)/<:T_ab(x)T_mn(y):>|. (3.1) ... If its components are always small compared to unity, then these fluctuations are small and we expect the semiclassical theory to hold. ... For simplicity, we will concentrate upon the coincidence limit, x -> y, of the purely temporal component ... Delta(x) = |(<:T00^2(x):> - <:T00(x):>^2)/<:T00^2(x):>|. (3.2) The local energy density fluctuations are small when Delta << 1, which we take to be a measure of the validity of the semiclassical theory. Note that we have used normal ordering with respect to the Minkowski vacuum state to define the various operators.' p.11-12: (3.43) Delta' = (<:T00^2:> - rho^2)/rho^2 = (1/8)[(rho+xi1+xi2+xi3)^2 + ...]; (3.44) Delta' = Delta/(1-Delta), Delta = Delta'/(1+Delta'). Sec. V: curved space 'will require a renormalization procedure for quartic operator products in such spacetimes, which has not yet been developed'; averaging 'introduces an arbitrary length or time scale'.
published_hypotheses: H1 PROPOSAL, not derivation: 'We propose that the extent to which the semiclassical approximation is violated can be measured by' Delta. It is motivated by Ford (1982) on graviton emission. No theorem bounds the error of G = 8 pi G <T> by Delta.
H2 The full measure is (3.1): all components, at two points x and y. The theory is expected to hold 'if its components are always small', which is a sufficiency-type expectation.
H3 Delta(x) in (3.2) is a reduction of (3.1) made 'for simplicity': the coincidence limit and the 00 component only.
H4 Every operator, including the quartic :T00^2:, is normal-ordered against the Minkowski vacuum, on a flat spacetime background.
H5 (3.2) has an absolute value. (3.44) tacitly assumes <:T00^2:> >= rho^2 and <:T00^2:> > 0.

H6 The examples use a massless scalar in flat spacetime, in single-mode number-state superpositions, squeezed states and the Casimir vacuum. The Casimir bound (3.45) assumes a diagonal <:d_A phi d_B phi:> and the Wick condition phi+|psi> = <psi|phi- = 0 (vacua).
H7 Scope limits in 1993: the curved-space quartic renormalisation 'has not yet been developed', and a smeared Delta needs a scale KF call 'arbitrary'.

KF's own vac+2 state breaks that at eps = 1, cos2th = -1, where rho = (2+sqrt2)K > 0 and rho^2/<:T^2:> = 1.9428: KF's Delta is +0.9428 and the tree's form gives -0.9428 (C2d-e). The absolute value is inactive on rho < 0 (C3a-b) and on every zero-mean Gaussian state (C5c), so no tree conclusion moves. The only visible site is the unrestricted formula at fluctuation.py:38-39.

KF only PROPOSE Delta as 'a measure'. The tree's wording at fluctuation.py:17-18 ('their criterion for the semiclassical equation to hold') is faithful.

audits.lacked_data:
The result is a definition plus a proposed criterion, with no empirical input. No measured datum was lacking and none has moved. What KF lacked in 1993 was theory, and they said so themselves.
(a) Curved-space renormalisation of quartic products. Perez & Sudarsky (2026) have since supplied it by the OPE. They find squeezed vacua fail the criterion and agree 'in general lines' with KF. This is evidence that having it does not overturn KF's qualitative conclusion.
(b) A principled averaging scale. The tree says the corridor has its own (fluctuation.py:110-113).
(c) A derivation of Delta as the actual error of G = 8 pi G <T>. None has appeared. Instead the criterion was refined by back-reaction stability (Hu-Roura-Verdaguer 2004, citing Hu-Phillips) or replaced by linear response (Anderson et al. 2002), under which flat space is stable although its Gaussian states have Delta of order 1.
That supports M's suspicion in one narrow sense: the validity criterion is incomplete. It ignores back reaction, and it is sign-blind, condemning thermal radiation at Delta = 2/5 (C7). It is no evidence that the definition or any flat-space value is wrong. Every internal identity checks exactly (C1, C4, C5), and the printed discrepancies are algebra or typography against v1, not missing data.

audits.published_statement: KF gr-qc/9304008 v1 Sec. V, verbatim from the saved excerpt: 'The analysis in this paper was restricted to a flat spacetime background. In this case, the expectation values of quartic operators which appear in the dimensionless measure of the fluctuations, Delta, or in the Langevin equation, Eq.(4.27), may be defined in terms of normal ordered products. The generalization of this analysis to curved spacetime backgrounds will require a renormalization procedure for quartic operator products in such spacetimes, which has not yet been developed. Note that an alternative approach to fluctuations is to discuss only averaged quantities. If we were to average fields over finite space or time intervals, then we could define a quantity similar to Delta without invoking normal ordering. ... this procedure suffers from the defect that it introduces an arbitrary length or time scale into the problem.'
published_hypotheses: H1: the remark is about the POINTWISE quartic expectation values in Delta (3.2) and in the Langevin equation (4.27). In flat space these are defined by normal ordering with respect to the Minkowski vacuum.
H2: the background is curved (non-Minkowski), so there is no preferred vacuum to normal-order against.
H3: the remark is TIME-INDEXED. 'has not yet been developed' describes the literature as of Feb/Apr 1993.
H4: KF state their own scope exclusion. AVERAGED quantities can be defined 'without invoking normal ordering'. Their objection to averaging is the arbitrary scale it introduces, not renormalisation.
H5: the field is a free, massless, minimally coupled scalar (Lagrangian (2.1)).
hypothesis_drift: FAITHFUL: fluctuation.py:114-116 quotes the sentence verbatim and dates it ('Their words, 1993'). It matches the saved source text string for string (checks Q0a-Q0c). The canonical hypotheses 'curved spacetime' and 'status of the literature as of 1993' match H2 and H3.

audits.lacked_data: What Kuo & Ford lacked was not a measured datum but a mathematical construction: renormalised coincident quartic products in curved spacetime. published_hypotheses: UNREAD at source. The hypotheses below are the ones the formula provably needs (re-derived here); they are not quoted from Le:

hypothesis_drift: DRIFT FROM THE SOURCE CANNOT BE CHECKED: with 2606.22531 unread, no drift between Le's printed hypotheses and the tree's use can be established or ruled out. The items below compare the hypotheses the formula provably needs with how the tree uses it.

IMPLICIT, and not named among the canonical hypotheses: H3 static equilibrium (wall.py:12-14, 41-47). 'The dec margin is therefore untouched' and 'independent of the equation-of-state slope' are TRUE of the equilibrium margin, since sigma_0 and p_0 contain no beta^2 (C6). Off equilibrium, though, the margin moves with beta^2 at first order: d(sigma-p)/dR|_R0 = (1-beta^2)(-2(sigma_0+p_0)/R_0), and d/dbeta^2 = (1-s)(3s+1)/(8 pi R^2 s) != 0 (C7). So for the oscillating stiff wall that wall.py builds, the margin during an excursion depends on beta^2. This is a hypothesis to name, not a refutation of wall.py's text, which speaks of the static margin.

EXTERIOR WEAKENED TO ITS STATIC LIMIT (wall.py:254-260 statics(); warpshell.py:18). Le's realized exterior is the Kinnersley photon rocket, which radiates outgoing null dust. Eq (17) as reproduced is the non-radiating Minkowski/Schwarzschild junction, i.e. lambda = aR/c^2 = 0. The tree itself records that for the radiating wall the dec window shrinks as lambda grows: 'lambda <~ (24/25 - x)/2  empirical dec envelope, not an inequality' (warpshell.py:91, 189). So 'no cost in dec margin' (wall.py:12-13) is established here only at lambda = 0.

WINDOW EDGES (wall.py:47, 'surface dec iff x < 24/25'). The margin is zero at s = 1/5 (x = 24/25) and at s = 1 (x = 0, no shell), and positive exactly on 0 < x < 24/25 (z3, C5). So strict dec holds iff 0 < x < 24/25, and non-strict dec holds on 0 < x <= 24/25. warpshell.py:86 says 'surface dec strict', which is the precise reading. This is a wording point only.

NOT A DRIFT, recorded because the canonical entry lists it as a hypothesis: 'Type I surface stress with p > 0' (wall.py:258-260) is not an extra assumption. p_0 = (1-s)^2/(16 pi R s) > 0 for every 0 < x < 1 (z3, C5).

NOT A DRIFT: the thin-shell window 24/25 is not the operative one. wall.py uses X_TANGENTIAL = 4/5 for the realized tangential-pressure wall (wall.py:244; warpshell.py:87) and correctly records 'the thin-shell dec window 24/25 is NOT' below x* = 0.8437 (wall.py:554).

DISCREPANCY IN THE TREE'S OWN CHECK, recorded and not repaired: wall.py:527-528 asserts 'dec margin is identical for every beta^2 (it is junction-fixed)' via len({round(dec_margin_scaled(0.3), 12)}) == 1. The claim itself still holds by construction (statics() takes no beta^2; C6), so nothing it guards is false.

audits.published_statement: Abstract p.1: 'The absolute frequencies of both transitions are also presented, each with a relative standard uncertainty of 6 x 10^-16 ... mu-dot/mu = 0.2(1.1) x 10^-16 year^-1 ... alpha-dot/alpha = -0.7(2.1) x 10^-17 year^-1.' p.1: 'the first direct measurement of the ratio between the E3 and E2 optical transition frequencies in 171Yb+, with fractional uncertainty 3 x 10^-16.' p.1: absolute frequencies 'are now limited by Cs primary standards.' p.3: 'nu_E3/nu_E2 = 0.932 829 404 530 964 65(31)'. The Table I totals (x1e-16) are E2 6.13, E3 5.79 and ratio 3.36. p.4: 'r-dot/r = (A_1 - A_2) alpha-dot/alpha + (B_1 - B_2) mu-dot/mu. The sensitivity coefficients A_i ... are: A_E3 = -5.95 [34], A_E2 = 0.88 [35], and A_Cs = 2.83 [36]. Dependence on mu-dot arises through the nuclear magnetic moment and is negligible for optical transitions (the sensitivity coefficient B_E3 = B_E2 = 0). As the 133Cs nuclear g-factor has negligible sensitivity to changes in the strong interaction [37, 38], an AFM history can also be interpreted to set constraints on mu-dot/mu (B_Cs = -1).' Also p.4: mu = m_p/m_e, and the limits hold 'on the assumption of local position invariance and that any time-variation is linear'.
published_hypotheses: H-MU: mu = m_p/m_e (p.4).
H-LIN: frequencies respond linearly to the constants, r-dot/r = (A_1-A_2) alpha-dot/alpha + (B_1-B_2) mu-dot/mu (p.4). This is a power-law dependence alpha^A mu^B.
H-AOPT: A_E3 = -5.95, A_E2 = 0.88 and A_Cs = 2.83 are atomic-structure calculations taken from refs [34]-[36] (1999-2008). They are not measured in this paper.
H-BOPT: B_E3 = B_E2 = 0 because an optical transition's mu-dependence 'is negligible' (p.4). This is an approximation, not an identity.
H-GCS: B_Cs = -1 rests on the premise that 'the 133Cs nuclear g-factor has negligible sensitivity to changes in the strong interaction [37, 38]' (p.4).
H-LPI: the mu-dot and alpha-dot limits assume local position invariance and linear time variation (p.4).

H-BUDGET: the 3e-16 and 6e-16 are the Table I totals (3.36, 6.13 and 5.79 x1e-16), from the systematics plus statistics over 105 h (E2) and 81 h (E3) in Feb-Mar 2014. The absolute totals are dominated by the Cs-referenced statistical term (4.77 and 5.35). Cs fountain systematics contribute 1.90 (Table II).

audits.published_statement: This was not read at source. Search-summary wording, which is NAMED-NOT-READ and is not quoted as source: 'On a compact space the total electric charge must be zero. audits.grade_evidence: F = rho v^2 A (coefficient 1, constant A, total proton density) is a generic ram-drag form and is internally correct under its stated hypotheses. Its arithmetic reproduces (2001.638 AU), and its floor label is TRUE under its own constant-A hypothesis: the exact solution has no finite stop and the relativistic forms diverge too. The label is also true under the pressure-balance law, where the true distance is 3L. But every READ magsail law holds on a smaller class than the tree uses: the area depends on velocity, only ions count (0.05-0.21 cm^-3, not 1), full reflection carries a factor 2, and the physics is non-relativistic with A = 0 unless I > beta x 1.55e6 A.
